definition_zh: 代码；密码；法典；编码
definition_en: a system of words or symbols used to represent information, a set of written rules or laws, or to write instructions for a computer
core_image: 把想法压缩成一串只有圈内人看得懂的符号
scene: 程序员盯着屏幕，把一段指令敲进编辑器。She wrote the code that runs the whole system.
sceneCN: 这里 code 指「代码」（第 1 个义项：计算机指令）；句意是她写下了运行整个系统的代码。

derivatives.zh: 编纂成法典；整理成系统

senses.title: Instructions for a computer
senses.definition: a set of instructions written for a computer program
senses.definitionCN: 为计算机程序编写的一组指令
senses.example: The code crashed when the file was too large.
senses.exampleCN: 文件太大时，这段代码崩溃了。
senses.why: A machine cannot read our words, so we hand it a private alphabet.
senses.whyCN: 机器读不懂人的语言，于是我们交给它一套私密字母表。

senses.title: A secret system of signs
senses.definition: a system of letters or symbols used to keep a message secret
senses.definitionCN: 用来保密信息的字母或符号系统
senses.example: The spy refused to give up the code.
senses.exampleCN: 那名间谍拒绝交出密码。
senses.why: Codes once kept messages safe from anyone without the key.
senses.whyCN: 密码曾让没有钥匙的人无法读懂信息。

senses.title: A set of written rules
senses.definition: a written set of laws or rules that govern behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 规范行为的一整套成文法律或规则
senses.example: Every member must follow the club's code.
senses.exampleCN: 每位成员都必须遵守俱乐部的准则。
senses.why: Law is also a code: signs arranged so that people can read what is allowed.
senses.whyCN: 法律也是一种代码：符号排好，让人读出什么被允许。

intro.en: Code traces back to Latin codex, the wooden tablet used for writing.
intro.cn: code 上溯拉丁语 codex，即用来书写的木板书板。

items.en: Codex meant a block of wood and then a tablet for writing.
items.cn: codex 本指一块木头，后指书写用的板。

items.en: A codex of laws held rules in one ordered book.
items.cn: 一部法典把规则收在一本有序的书里。

items.en: French code carried the legal sense into English.
items.cn: 法语 code 把法律义带进了英语。

items.en: The word spread from law to any organised set of signs.
items.cn: 这个词从法律扩展到任何有组织的符号系统。

items.en: Computing made code the everyday word for program text.
items.cn: 计算机让 code 成为程序文本的日常说法。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words that differ from code by one letter, while the meaning group covers secret writing and instruction sets.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 code 只差一两个字母的短词，近义组涉及密文与指令集。

entries.definition: a shape with a round base and a point
entries.definitionCN: 底面为圆、顶端带尖的形状

entries.definition: a long thin flexible rope
entries.definitionCN: 细长而有弹性的绳

entries.definition: to deal successfully with a hard situation
entries.definitionCN: 成功应付困难局面

entries.definition: a secret way of writing messages
entries.definitionCN: 书写密文的秘密方式

entries.definition: a set of instructions that makes a computer work
entries.definitionCN: 让计算机工作的一组指令

entries.definition: a rule made by a government for all people
entries.definitionCN: 政府为所有人制定的规则

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the wooden tablet, the secret letter and the lines a programmer types.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把木板书板、密信和程序员敲下的行行字符连在一起。

normal.en: A codex was a wooden tablet, so code begins with something written down.
normal.cn: codex 是木板书板，所以 code 的起点是写下来的东西。

normal.en: Laws were gathered into codes long before computers existed.
normal.cn: 早在计算机出现之前，法律就被汇编成法典。

normal.en: A code keeps a message closed to outsiders, like a locked box.
normal.cn: 密码把信息对局外人锁住，像一只上锁的箱子。

normal.en: Add the prefix de and decode means opening that box again.
normal.cn: 加上前缀 de，decode 就是把那只箱子重新打开。

normal.en: Code and decode sit at opposite ends of one message.
normal.cn: code 与 decode 位于同一条信息的两端。

abstract.en: Picture a monk copying laws onto a thick wooden tablet.
abstract.cn: 想象一位修士把法律条文抄到厚厚的木板上。

abstract.en: Picture a page of symbols that only one reader can unlock.
abstract.cn: 想象一页符号，只有一位读者能把它解开。

abstract.en: Picture green lines of text scrolling down a dark screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一行行绿色字符在暗屏上向下滚动。

examples.en: He spent the night fixing a bug in the code.
examples.cn: 他花了一整夜修复代码里的一个错误。

examples.en: The letter was written in a code that nobody could read.
examples.cn: 这封信是用没人能读懂的密码写的。

examples.en: The new code on dress makes the office more relaxed.
examples.cn: 新的着装准则让办公室氛围更轻松。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 code 记成一本锁起来的符号册：翻开来是指令，锁起来是密码。

root: 源自拉丁语 codex（木板书板），经法语 code 进入英语，由成文法典扩展为符号系统与计算机指令。

sensesIntro.en: From a written tablet to a book of laws, then to hidden signs and machine instructions.
sensesIntro.cn: 从书写的木板，到成文法典，再到隐秘符号与机器指令。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a string of signs that carries meaning only to those who hold the key.
core.cn: 核心意象：一串只有持钥匙者才读得懂的符号。

branches.en: Machine code is the newest and most common sense today.
branches.cn: 机器代码是今天最新也最常用的义项。

branches.en: A cipher hides a message behind unfamiliar signs.
branches.cn: 密码用陌生的符号把信息藏起来。

branches.en: A code of law arranges rules in one readable order.
branches.cn: 法典把规则排成一个可读的顺序。

branches.en: Both senses rest on a fixed system of signs.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在固定的符号系统上。

branches.en: A programmer and a lawmaker both write codes that others must follow.
branches.cn: 程序员与立法者都在写别人必须遵循的代码。

intro.en: Code takes Latin prefixes easily, so its family is built on en-, de- and -ify.
intro.cn: code 很容易接拉丁前缀，家族靠 en-、de- 与 -ify 构建。

latinIntro.en: The base codex is Latin for a writing tablet, and codex still names an ancient book.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 codex 在拉丁语中指书写板，今天 codex 仍指古籍抄本。

items.meaning: more than one code, or he writes instructions
items.example: The two codes must match exactly.
items.exampleCN: 两套代码必须完全一致。

items.meaning: put into a code or written as a program
items.example: The message was coded before it was sent.
items.exampleCN: 这条信息在发送前已被加密。

items.meaning: the work of writing computer programs
items.example: Coding takes patience more than speed.
items.exampleCN: 编程更需要耐心而不是速度。

items.meaning: a person who writes computer code
items.example: She hired a coder for the new app.
items.exampleCN: 她为这款新应用请了一位程序员。

items.meaning: to change information into a code
items.example: The device encodes every call.
items.exampleCN: 这台设备把每通电话都编码。

items.meaning: to turn a code back into plain meaning
items.meaningCN: 把代码还原为明白的意思
items.example: They needed a key to decode the file.
items.exampleCN: 他们需要一把钥匙来解码这个文件。

items.meaning: to arrange rules into a clear system
items.meaningCN: 把规则整理成清晰的体系
items.example: The team codified its safety rules.
items.exampleCN: 这个团队把安全规则编纂成文。

items.meaning: the act of arranging rules into a code
items.example: The codification of the law took years.
items.exampleCN: 这部法律的编纂花了数年。

items.meaning: a pattern of lines read by a machine
items.example: The cashier scanned the barcode.
items.exampleCN: 收银员扫了条形码。

items.meaning: a group of letters and numbers used in an address
items.meaningCN: 地址中使用的邮政编码
items.example: Please write your postcode clearly.
items.exampleCN: 请把邮政编码写清楚。

latinEntries.meaning: a wooden tablet or a bound manuscript
latinEntries.example: The oldest codex in the library is under glass.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 馆中最古老的抄本放在玻璃罩下。

definition_zh: n. 编纂，法典化；（规则、知识的）系统整理
definition_en: the act of arranging laws or rules into an organised code or system
core_image: 散落的条例被逐条抄进一本厚法典
scene: 委员会完成了整套税法规定的编纂。The committee completed the codification of the tax rules.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：codification 指编纂；句意是委员会完成了整套税法规定的编纂。

senses.title: Arranging rules into a code
senses.definition: the act of putting laws or rules into one ordered code
senses.definitionCN: 把法律或规则整理成一部有序法典的行为
senses.example: The codification of the tax law took years.
senses.exampleCN: 税法的编纂花了数年。
senses.why: Latin codex means a book, and -ficare means to make.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 codex 意为书，-ficare 意为使成为。

senses.title: A systematic collection
senses.definition: an organised collection of knowledge or customs
senses.definitionCN: 对知识或习俗的有序汇编
senses.example: Her book is a codification of local customs.
senses.exampleCN: 她的书是当地习俗的系统汇编。
senses.why: The legal sense widened to any ordered body.
senses.whyCN: 法律义扩展到任何有序体系。

intro.en: Codification makes a book out of scattered rules.
intro.cn: codification 就是把散落的规定做成一部书。

items.en: Codex means a bound book.
items.cn: codex 意为装订成册的书。

items.en: Facere means to make.
items.cn: facere 意为做、使。

items.en: Jurists speak of the codification of law.
items.cn: 十九世纪法学家谈法律编纂。

items.en: The word covers rules, customs and knowledge.
items.cn: 现代该词涵盖规则、习俗与知识。

items.en: Even data can be codified into systems.
items.cn: 数字时代连数据也能被整理成体系。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cod- start; the near-meaning group names organising and law-making.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cod- 开头；近义组列出整理与立法。

entries.definition: An ordered set of rules or signs.
entries.definitionCN: 法典；代码。

entries.definition: To arrange into a code.
entries.definitionCN: 编纂。

entries.definition: Writing instructions for a computer.
entries.definitionCN: 编程。

entries.definition: The act of putting into a system.
entries.definitionCN: 系统化。

entries.definition: The act of collecting material.
entries.definitionCN: 汇编。

entries.definition: Laws made by a parliament.
entries.definitionCN: 立法。

normalIntro.en: Codex is a book: codification books the rules.
normalIntro.cn: codex 是书：codification 就是把规则装订成书。

normal.en: Codex means book.
normal.cn: codex 意为书。

normal.en: -fication means making.
normal.cn: -fication 意为使成为。

normal.en: Scattered rules become one code.
normal.cn: 零散规则变成一部法典。

normal.en: Lawyers love codification.
normal.cn: 法学家喜爱编纂。

normal.en: Customs can be codified too.
normal.cn: 习俗也能被整理成文。

abstract.en: A library of loose pages bound at last.
abstract.cn: 终于装订起来的一堆散页。

abstract.en: Order written down.
abstract.cn: 被写下来的秩序。

abstract.en: Many voices, one book.
abstract.cn: 许多声音，一本书。

examples.en: The codification of the old customs took a decade.
examples.cn: 旧习俗的整理成文花了十年。

examples.en: Codification makes the rules easier to teach.
examples.cn: 编纂让规则更容易教授。

examples.en: She studied the codification of Roman law.
examples.cn: 她研究罗马法的法典化。

dict_mnemonic.text: codex（书）+ -fication（使成为）→ 把规则做成书，即编纂。

root: 拉丁 codex（书册）+ facere（做）→ 法语 codification → 英语 codification

sensesIntro.en: Law first, customs second: the same act of putting things into ordered form.
sensesIntro.cn: 先法律，后习俗：同样是把事物整理成有序形态的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: loose sheets entered one by one into a bound code
core.cn: 核心意象：散页被逐条抄进装订成册的法典

branches.en: A jurist copying tax rules into one book.
branches.cn: 把税则抄进一本书的法学家。

branches.en: A parliament approving a single code.
branches.cn: 议会通过一部统一法典。

branches.en: A scholar listing local customs.
branches.cn: 列举地方习俗的学者。

branches.en: A manual organising scattered knowledge.
branches.cn: 整理零散知识的手册。

branches.en: Any loose body of rules made orderly.
branches.cn: 任何零散规则被整理有序。

intro.en: Codification is built from a word for a book; the list adds writing and law pieces.
intro.cn: codification 由「书」之词构成；下面列出书写与法律词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin codex is a book, lex is law, and norma is a rule.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 codex 意为书，lex 意为法，norma 意为规则。

definition_zh: n. 腔肠动物（刺胞动物的旧称）
definition_en: an old name for a simple water animal such as a jellyfish or coral, with a hollow body
core_image: 海葵张开触手，身体是一根空心的囊
scene: 水母和海葵都属于腔肠动物这一古老类群。Jellyfish and sea anemones belong to the old group called coelenterates.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：coelenterate 指腔肠动物；句意是水母和海葵都属于腔肠动物这一古老类群。

senses.title: An old name for cnidarians
senses.definition: an older name for jellyfish, corals and their relatives
senses.definitionCN: 水母、珊瑚及其近亲的旧称
senses.example: Coelenterates include jellyfish and corals.
senses.exampleCN: 腔肠动物包括水母与珊瑚。
senses.why: Greek koilos means hollow and enteron means intestine.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 koilos 意为空，enteron 意为肠。

senses.title: A two-layered simple animal
senses.definition: an animal with two cell layers and a single body opening
senses.definitionCN: 只有两层细胞、单个身体开口的动物
senses.example: A coelenterate has one opening for food and waste.
senses.exampleCN: 腔肠动物只有一个进食排废的开口。
senses.why: The hollow gut gave the group its name.
senses.whyCN: 空心的肠腔给了这一类群名字。

intro.en: The name says hollow gut, the shape that defines these animals.
intro.cn: 这个名字意为「空肠」，正是这类动物的形状。

items.en: Koilos means hollow.
items.cn: koilos 意为空的。

items.en: Enteron means intestine or gut.
items.cn: enteron 意为肠。

items.en: Zoologists name the group for its hollow body.
items.cn: 十九世纪动物学家因其中空身体命名该类群。

items.en: The name gives way to cnidarian in modern science.
items.cn: 二十世纪学界改称刺胞动物。

items.en: Coelenterate survives as an older term.
items.cn: 现代它作为旧称保留。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the coel- or enter- shape; the near-meaning group names the modern group and its members.
note.cn: 形近组共享 coel- 或 enter- 词形；近义组列出现代类群与成员。

entries.definition: A hollow space inside an animal.
entries.definitionCN: 体腔。

entries.definition: Relating to the intestines.
entries.definitionCN: 肠的。

entries.definition: Relating to the abdomen.
entries.definitionCN: 腹部的。

entries.definition: A jellyfish or coral animal.
entries.definitionCN: 刺胞动物。

entries.definition: A soft see-through sea animal.
entries.definitionCN: 水母。

entries.definition: A fixed tube-shaped sea animal.
entries.definitionCN: 水螅体。

normalIntro.en: Coelenterate is Greek for hollow gut, the body plan of a jellyfish.
normalIntro.cn: coelenterate 是希腊语「空肠」，也就是水母的身体构造。

normal.en: Coel means hollow.
normal.cn: coel 意为空。

normal.en: Enteron means gut.
normal.cn: enteron 意为肠。

normal.en: A jellyfish is a hollow sea.
normal.cn: 水母就是一片空心的海。

normal.en: One opening serves mouth and waste.
normal.cn: 一个开口兼作口与排废。

normal.en: Modern science says cnidarian.
normal.cn: 现代科学称 cnidarian。

abstract.en: A stomach that swims.
abstract.cn: 会游泳的胃。

abstract.en: Water shaped into an animal.
abstract.cn: 被塑成动物的水。

abstract.en: A net of tentacles round a hollow.
abstract.cn: 围住空洞的一张触手网。

examples.en: The textbook still lists coelenterates in one chapter.
examples.cn: 这本教科书仍用一章讲腔肠动物。

examples.en: Coral is a coelenterate that builds reefs.
examples.cn: 珊瑚是筑礁的腔肠动物。

examples.en: Some coelenterates glow in the dark sea.
examples.cn: 有些腔肠动物在暗海里发光。

dict_mnemonic.text: coel（空）+ enter（肠）→ 身体像空心肠子，即腔肠动物。

root: 希腊 koilos（空）+ enteron（肠）→ 新拉丁 coelenterata → 英语 coelenterate

sensesIntro.en: One hollow gut names a whole old group of sea animals.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个空肠命名了一整类古老的海洋动物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hollow sac opening into a ring of tentacles
core.cn: 核心意象：空心囊开口围着一圈触手

branches.en: A jellyfish drifting in blue water.
branches.cn: 漂在蓝水中的水母。

branches.en: Sea anemones on a rock.
branches.cn: 礁石上的海葵。

branches.en: One opening taking food and waste.
branches.cn: 一个兼作进食与排废的开口。

branches.en: A two-layered body wall.
branches.cn: 两层的体壁。

branches.en: A simple hollow animal and its old name.
branches.cn: 简单的空心动物与它的旧名。

intro.cn: coelenterate 由希腊语「空」与「肠」组合；下面列出海洋动物词场的词缀。

items.exampleCN: 刺胞动物；刺细胞

definition_zh: v. 共存，同时存在；和平共处
definition_en: to exist at the same time, or to live together without conflict
core_image: 古寺与玻璃高楼在同一条街上相对而立
scene: 在这座城市里，古老寺庙与现代高楼并存。Ancient temples and modern towers coexist in this city.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：coexist 指共存；句意是在这座城市里，古老寺庙与现代高楼并存。

senses.title: To exist at the same time
senses.definition: to be present together at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 在同一时间共同存在
senses.example: Dinosaurs and early mammals coexisted.
senses.exampleCN: 恐龙与早期哺乳动物曾共存。
senses.why: Latin co means together and existere means to stand forth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 co 意为共同，existere 意为出现、存在。

senses.title: To live together peacefully
senses.definition: to live side by side without fighting
senses.definitionCN: 相邻而居而不冲突
senses.example: The two communities coexist without conflict.
senses.exampleCN: 两个社区没有冲突地共处。
senses.why: The neutral sense took on a political one.
senses.whyCN: 中性的「共存」带上了政治含义。

intro.en: Coexist puts together and exist into one word.

definition_zh: 认知；知觉、记忆、推理等心理过程的总称，也指一次认识活动
definition_en: the mental processes by which people perceive, remember, reason and know, or a single act of knowing
core_image: 脑中同时亮起感知、记忆与推理几盏灯，合起来照亮一个判断
scene: 志愿者看一张图三秒后回忆细节，再比较两种图案的差异。The volunteer recalls the details of a picture and then compares two patterns in the mind, a task designed to measure cognition.
sceneCN: 这里 cognition 指「知觉、记忆、推理等心理过程的总称」（第 1 个义项：把各种心智活动合在一起看）；句意为志愿者回忆图中细节并比较两种图案，这项任务用来测量认知。图中可辨识物件：图片、屏幕上的两种图案、秒表、记录表。

pos.zh: 认知；认识过程（不可数；指一次具体的认识活动时可数）

derivatives.zh: 认知主义（认为心智可作信息加工来研究）

senses.title: The whole set of mental processes
senses.definition: the collective name for perception, memory, reasoning, judgment and other ways of knowing
senses.definitionCN: 知觉、记忆、推理、判断等认识方式的集合名称
senses.example: The volunteer recalls details and compares patterns in one task.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者在一项任务中回忆细节并比较图案。
senses.why: cognition gathers several faculties under one word because they cooperate in every real judgment; the noun names the team, not one player.
senses.whyCN: cognition 把几种官能收在一个词下，因为真实的判断总由它们协作完成；这个名词命名的是整支队伍，而不是单个队员。

senses.title: Cognitive ability
senses.definition: the capacity to perceive, remember and reason, measured in tests
senses.definitionCN: 在测验中衡量的知觉、记忆与推理能力
senses.example: The test scores cognition separately from language.
senses.exampleCN: 这项测验把认知与语言分开计分。
senses.why: a faculty can be measured like a muscle, so the same noun shifts from the process to the capacity that supports it.
senses.whyCN: 官能可以像肌肉一样被测量，因此同一个名词从「过程」转为支撑过程的「能力」。

senses.title: A single act of knowing
senses.definition: one instance of coming to know or noticing something, countable in philosophy
senses.definitionCN: 一次得知或察觉某事的行为，在哲学中可数
senses.example: Each cognition begins with a distinction between self and object.
senses.exampleCN: 每一次认识都始于自我与对象的区分。
senses.why: philosophy counts acts rather than faculties, so the mass noun gains a plural and a beginning and an end.
senses.whyCN: 哲学计数的是行为而非官能，因此这个不可数名词获得了复数，也有了开头与结尾。

senses.title: Perception as the entry gate
senses.definition: the part of cognition that takes in sensory information
senses.definitionCN: 认知中接收感官信息的那一部分
senses.example: Colour cognition starts with the eye but does not end there.
senses.exampleCN: 颜色认知始于眼睛，却不止于眼睛。
senses.why: nothing enters the mind without a sense channel, so perception is cognition at its boundary with the world.
senses.whyCN: 没有感官通道，任何东西都进不了心智，因此知觉是认知与世界相接的边界。

senses.title: Memory and mental representation
senses.definition: the storing and reactivating of information inside the mind
senses.definitionCN: 信息在心内储存并被重新调用的过程
senses.example: Recalling the picture depends on memory as much as on perception.
senses.exampleCN: 回忆那张图既依赖知觉，也依赖记忆。
senses.why: once information is taken in, it must be kept in some form; representation is the internal stand-in for the absent thing.
senses.whyCN: 信息一旦被接收，就必须以某种形式保存；表征就是缺席之物在心内的替身。

senses.title: Reasoning and judgment
senses.definition: the manipulation of representations to reach a conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 对表征进行操作以得出一个结论
senses.example: Comparing the two patterns requires reasoning about difference.
senses.exampleCN: 比较两种图案需要对差异进行推理。
senses.why: cognition is not only storage; it also transforms what is stored, and that transformation is what we call thinking.
senses.whyCN: 认知不只是储存，它还会改造所存之物，而这种改造就是我们所说的思考。

senses.title: The field of cognitive science
senses.definition: the interdisciplinary study of mind, spanning psychology, linguistics, neuroscience and computation
senses.definitionCN: 跨越心理学、语言学、神经科学与计算的心智交叉研究
senses.example: Cognition is the central object of the new institute.
senses.exampleCN: 认知是这家新研究所的核心研究对象。
senses.why: a phenomenon can name a discipline: what is studied becomes the label on the door of the department that studies it.
senses.whyCN: 一种现象可以命名一门学科：被研究的东西，最终成了研究它的那间办公室门上的标签。

senses.title: Social and situated cognition
senses.definition: knowing as it happens in interaction with other people and with a setting
senses.definitionCN: 在与他人的互动及具体环境中发生的认识
senses.example: Social cognition explains why a frown changes our judgment.
senses.exampleCN: 社会认知解释了为什么一个皱眉会改变我们的判断。
senses.why: the mind rarely works alone; when researchers looked at real settings, the unit of study grew from one head to a pair and a room.
senses.whyCN: 心智很少独自工作；研究者转向真实情境后，研究单位便从一个脑袋扩大为一对人和一个房间。

intro.en: Cognition comes from Latin cognitio 'a getting to know', from cognoscere 'to get to know', itself com- plus gnoscere 'to know'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cognition 来自拉丁 cognitio「得知、认识」，源自动词 cognoscere「认识、了解」，后者由 com- 加 gnoscere「知道」构成。年代为约数。

items.en: Gnoscere meant 'to know, recognize'; it belongs to the old root for knowing that also appears in English know and in Greek gnosis.
items.cn: gnoscere 意为「知道、认出」；它属于古老的「知」词根，英语 know 与希腊语 gnosis 也在此列。

items.en: Com- 'thoroughly, together' plus gnoscere produced cognoscere, 'to get to know, learn, recognize'; the prefix here intensifies rather than adds a partner.
items.cn: com-「彻底、一起」加 gnoscere 构成 cognoscere，意为「得知、了解、认出」；这里的前缀起加强作用，而非增加一个伙伴。

items.en: The noun cognitio 'a getting to know, acquaintance, knowledge' was formed on the participle stem cognit-.
items.cn: 名词 cognitio「得知、认识、知识」由分词词干 cognit- 构成。

items.en: English took cognition from Latin or French in the fifteenth century; early spellings included cognicion.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪从拉丁语或法语借入 cognition；早期拼写包括 cognicion。

items.en: From the twentieth century the word names the whole information-processing side of the mind, and cognitive science was founded as a field in the 1970s.
items.cn: 20 世纪起，这个词命名心智中整个信息加工的一面；认知科学作为学科在 20 世纪 70 年代确立。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest English citation is not firmly dated, and the exact force of com- in cognoscere is debated between 'thoroughly' and 'together'.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：最早的英语书证没有确切年代；com- 在 cognoscere 中究竟表示「彻底」还是「一起」，学界有争论。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same knowing root; group two holds neighboring mental terms that are often used loosely as synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组是同一「知」词根构成的词；第二组是常被宽松当作同义词的心智术语。

entries.definition: Relating to cognition; cognition is the noun, cognitive the adjective that must modify something.
entries.definitionCN: 与认知有关的；cognition 是名词，cognitive 是必须修饰某物的形容词。

entries.definition: The act of identifying something as known before; re- 'again' adds the return of a previous knowing.
entries.definitionCN: 认出某物曾见过；re-「再次」加入「重新知道」的意思。

entries.definition: Awareness or notice, especially in law; it is the same Latin source reshaped in French, not a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 知晓、注意，尤用于法律；同一拉丁来源经法语改形，并非不同词根。

entries.definition: A word related by descent; it joins co- with gnatus 'born', so its second element means birth, not knowing.
entries.definitionCN: 同源词；它把 co- 与 gnatus「出生」结合，第二部分意为出生，而非知道。

entries.definition: The taking in of sensory information; it is one stage of cognition, not the whole chain.
entries.definitionCN: 接收感官信息；是认知的一个阶段，而非整条链条。

entries.definition: An idea or the activity of thinking; cognition is the broader scientific term for all such activity.
entries.definitionCN: 一个想法或思考活动；cognition 是对所有此类活动的更宽泛的科学术语。

entries.definition: Thinking that moves from premises to conclusions; it is one kind of cognition with a strict order.
entries.definitionCN: 从前提走向结论的思考；是有严格顺序的一种认知。

entries.definition: The state of being awake and aware; cognition can be studied without solving the puzzle of consciousness.
entries.definitionCN: 清醒并有所觉察的状态；认知可以在不解决意识难题的情况下被研究。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.

normal.en: com- 'thoroughly' + gnoscere 'know' = get to know thoroughly; the same root appears in know and gnosis.
normal.cn: com-「彻底」+ gnoscere「知道」= 彻底了解；同一词根也出现在 know 与 gnosis 中。

normal.en: The family runs cognition, cognitive, cognitively, cognize and cognizance.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cognition、cognitive、cognitively、cognize 与 cognizance。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scope: human cognition, social cognition, cognition and memory.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：人类认知、社会认知、认知与记忆。

normal.en: Cognition is the umbrella; perception, memory and reasoning are its parts.
normal.cn: cognition 是伞；perception、memory 与 reasoning 是伞下的各部分。

normal.en: Do not confuse cognition with cognate: the first root means know, the second means born.
normal.cn: 不要把 cognition 与 cognate 混淆：前者词根意为「知」，后者意为「出生」。

examples.cn: 社会认知研究我们如何解读他人的意图。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可个尼神」——脑子里几盏灯一起亮，才认得清 → 认知

root: 拉丁 cognitio「认识」← cognoscere「得知」= com-（彻底）+ gnoscere「知道」；与 know、gnosis 同出古老的「知」词根。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses separate what is usually bundled: the faculty, its measurable strength, a single act, perception, memory, reasoning, the science, and knowing in company.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把平日捆在一起的东西分开：官能、可测的强度、单次行为、知觉、记忆、推理、学科，以及与他人共处的认识。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several lamps lit at once, each showing a different face of the same object.
core.cn: 核心意象：几盏灯同时亮起，各自照出同一对象的不同侧面。

branches.en: THE WHOLE AND ITS STRENGTH: the team of faculties, then the muscle measured by a test.
branches.cn: 整体与强度：先是一组官能，再是被测验衡量的那块肌肉。

branches.en: ONE ACT: philosophy cuts the stream into countable moments of knowing.
branches.cn: 单次行为：哲学把连续流切成可计数的「知」的瞬间。

branches.en: ENTRY AND STORE: perception lets the world in, memory keeps it.
branches.cn: 入口与储存：知觉让世界进来，记忆把它留住。

branches.en: TRANSFORM: reasoning rearranges what perception and memory supply.
branches.cn: 改造：推理重新排列知觉与记忆提供的东西。

branches.en: LABEL AND SETTING: the process becomes a department, and the lone mind becomes a pair.
branches.cn: 标签与情境：过程变成学科，孤单的心智变成一对人。

intro.en: Cognition is a Latin prefix-root noun: com- plus gnoscere plus -tion. The root carries the idea of knowing, the prefix the idea of thoroughness.
intro.cn: cognition 是拉丁前缀加词根的名词：com- 加 gnoscere 再加 -tion。词根承载「知」，前缀承载「彻底」。

latinIntro.en: Latin gnoscere 'to know' gives cognoscere and cognitio; English draws cognition, cognitive, cognizance and recognize from the same line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 gnoscere「知道」生成 cognoscere 与 cognitio；英语由此得到 cognition、cognitive、cognizance 与 recognize。

items.example: Before n the prefix is written com-, not con-.
items.exampleCN: 在 n 之前，这个前缀写作 com-，不是 con-。

items.example: The root survives in gnosis and diagnosis.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根留在 gnosis 与 diagnosis 中。

items.meaning: to get to know, learn, recognize
items.example: Cognoscere is the source of the whole English family.
items.exampleCN: cognoscere 是整个英语词族的来源。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb of knowing into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「知」的动词变成名词。

items.meaning: the act or faculty of knowing
items.example: Cognition covers perception, memory and reasoning.
items.exampleCN: 认知涵盖知觉、记忆与推理。

items.example: Cognitive tests measure more than memory.
items.exampleCN: 认知测验测量的不止记忆。

items.example: The court took cognizance of the report.
items.exampleCN: 法院注意到了这份报告。

items.example: She recognized the melody at once.
items.exampleCN: 她立刻认出了这段旋律。

items.example: Cognate words share an ancestor, not a meaning.
items.exampleCN: 同源词共享祖词，而非共享词义。

definition_zh: 认知的；与知觉、记忆、推理等思维过程有关的
definition_en: relating to the mental processes of perceiving, remembering, reasoning and knowing
core_image: 一张脑内地图上标着看、记、想三个相连的节点
scene: 老师让学生先记住一串数字，再做一道逻辑题，比较两种任务的表现。The teacher asks students to memorize a string of digits and then solve a logic puzzle, comparing their performance on two cognitive tasks.
sceneCN: 这里 cognitive 指「与思维过程有关的」（第 1 个义项：知觉、记忆、推理这类活动）；句意为老师让学生记数字再做逻辑题，比较两种认知任务的表现。图中可辨识物件：数字串、逻辑题、两块答题板、计时器。

pos.zh: 认知的；与思维过程有关的

derivatives.zh: 元认知的（对自己的思考进行思考）

senses.title: Relating to thinking processes
senses.definition: concerning perception, memory, reasoning or other mental processes
senses.definitionCN: 关乎知觉、记忆、推理或其他心理过程
senses.example: The teacher compares performance on two cognitive tasks.
senses.exampleCN: 老师比较两项认知任务的表现。
senses.why: the adjective adds -ive 'tending to' to the noun stem, so it describes anything that belongs to the business of knowing.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在名词词干后加 -ive「倾向于」，描述一切属于「认识」这件事的东西。

senses.title: Of cognitive psychology
senses.definition: belonging to the branch of psychology that studies mental processes
senses.definitionCN: 属于研究心理过程的心理学分支
senses.example: The lab runs a cognitive psychology experiment on attention.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室做了一项关于注意的认知心理学实验。
senses.why: a discipline needs an adjective for its own subject matter, and this word supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科需要为本学科的研究对象配一个形容词，这个词正好补上。

senses.title: Cognitive development
senses.definition: the growth of perception, memory and reasoning from infancy onward
senses.definitionCN: 从婴儿期起知觉、记忆与推理的发展
senses.example: Picture books support cognitive development in toddlers.
senses.exampleCN: 图画书有助于幼儿的认知发展。
senses.why: development adds time to cognition; the adjective marks which line of growth is being measured.
senses.whyCN: 发展给认知加上时间；这个形容词标明被测量的是哪一条成长线。

senses.title: Cognitive bias and cognitive load
senses.definition: used in fixed terms for systematic errors of judgment and for the mental effort a task demands
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定术语，指判断的系统性偏差以及任务所需的心智努力
senses.example: Long instructions raise cognitive load before the task begins.
senses.exampleCN: 冗长的说明在任务开始前就提高了认知负荷。
senses.why: once a field finds regular failure modes, it names them with the same adjective: bias in judging, load in working memory.
senses.whyCN: 一个领域发现规律性的失败模式后，就用同一个形容词命名它们：判断中的偏差、工作记忆中的负荷。

senses.title: Cognitive linguistics
senses.definition: relating to the approach that treats language as shaped by general mental processes
senses.definitionCN: 属于把语言视为一般心智过程之产物的研究取向
senses.example: Cognitive linguistics treats metaphor as ordinary thought.
senses.exampleCN: 认知语言学把隐喻视为日常思维。
senses.why: the adjective lets a whole school declare its base: language is not a separate module but part of cognition.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词让整个学派声明自己的立足点：语言不是独立模块，而是认知的一部分。

senses.title: Cognitive therapy
senses.definition: relating to treatment that works on thought patterns rather than only on behavior
senses.definitionCN: 属于针对思维模式而非只针对行为的治疗
senses.example: Cognitive therapy asks the patient to test a fearful belief.
senses.exampleCN: 认知疗法要求病人检验一个恐惧信念。
senses.why: if distorted thinking maintains distress, then changing the thinking is a route to changing the distress.
senses.whyCN: 如果扭曲的思维维持着痛苦，那么改变思维就是改变痛苦的一条路径。

senses.title: Belonging to cognitive science
senses.definition: relating to the interdisciplinary study of mind, information and computation
senses.definitionCN: 属于心智、信息与计算的交叉研究
senses.example: The programme combines cognitive and computational methods.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目结合认知方法与计算方法。
senses.why: the adjective becomes a badge of a field that borrows from psychology, linguistics, neuroscience and computing at once.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词成了一个领域的徽章，它同时借用心理学、语言学、神经科学与计算。

senses.title: Cognitive meaning in language
senses.definition: the conceptual content a word carries, as opposed to its emotional colouring
senses.definitionCN: 词语承载的概念内容，与情感色彩相对
senses.example: The cognitive meaning of home is a dwelling, not a feeling.
senses.exampleCN: 「家」这个词的认知意义是住所，而不是一种情感。
senses.why: linguists split meaning into what it denotes and what it evokes; the adjective labels the denotative half.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家把意义分为「指什么」与「唤起什么」；这个形容词标记前者。

intro.en: Cognitive is Medieval Latin cognitivus, built on the participle stem of cognoscere 'to get to know' plus -ivus. It entered English in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cognitive 是晚期拉丁 cognitivus，由 cognoscere「得知」的分词词干加 -ivus 构成。它在 16 世纪进入英语。年代为约数。

items.en: Cognoscere 'to get to know' joins com- 'thoroughly' to gnoscere 'to know'; its participle stem is cognit-.
items.cn: cognoscere「得知」把 com-「彻底」与 gnoscere「知道」结合；其分词词干为 cognit-。

items.en: Scholastic Latin formed cognitivus 'having the power of knowing' from cognit- plus the adjective suffix -ivus.
items.cn: 经院拉丁语由 cognit- 加形容词后缀 -ivus 构成 cognitivus，意为「具有认识能力的」。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the sixteenth century, at first in philosophical writing about the powers of the mind.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入这个形容词，最初用于讨论心智能力的哲学著作。

items.en: Cognitive psychology, cognitive science and cognitive therapy all took their names in the twentieth century, when the mind was studied as an information processor.
items.cn: 认知心理学、认知科学与认知疗法都在 20 世纪得名，当时心智被当作信息加工系统来研究。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest English citation is not precisely fixed, and the medieval coinage may have been influenced by Greek-derived models in scholastic Latin.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：最早的英语书证没有精确年代；这一中世纪新造词可能受经院拉丁语中希腊式构词模式的影响。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same knowing stem; group two holds adjectives about mental life with different scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同一「知」词干的形式；第二组是范围不同的心智形容词。

entries.definition: The processes themselves; cognitive is the adjective that describes them or the tasks that measure them.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程本身；cognitive 是描述这些过程或测量任务的形容词。

entries.definition: Knowing that something is the case; it means 'aware of', not 'relating to thinking processes'.
entries.definitionCN: 知道某事属实；意为「知晓」，不是「与思维过程有关」。

entries.definition: Relating to serious thought and learning; it comes from intellectus, another descendant of the same legere family.
entries.definitionCN: 与严肃思考及学识有关的；来自 intellectus，是同一 legere 词族的另一支。

entries.definition: Related by descent in language; its second element is gnatus 'born', so it is not about thinking.
entries.definitionCN: 语言上同源的；第二部分是 gnatus「出生」，与思维无关。

entries.definition: Relating to the mind in general, including emotion and will; cognitive is narrower and points to knowing.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指心智，包括情绪与意志；cognitive 更窄，指向「知」。

entries.definition: Relating to the senses and to what is taken in; perception is only the first stage of cognition.
entries.definitionCN: 与感官及所接收之物有关；知觉只是认知的第一阶段。

entries.definition: Following reason and logic; rational judges the quality of thinking, while cognitive only locates its domain.
entries.definitionCN: 遵循理性与逻辑；rational 评判思考的质量，cognitive 只标出所属领域。

entries.definition: Relating to psychology, including emotion, motivation and social behavior; cognitive covers only the knowing side.
entries.definitionCN: 与心理学有关，包含情绪、动机与社会行为；cognitive 只覆盖「知」的一面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: cognit- 'know' + -ive 'tending to': anything that belongs to the work of knowing.
normal.cn: cognit-「知」+ -ive「倾向于」：一切属于「认识」这件事的东西。

normal.en: The family runs cognition, cognitive, cognitively, cognitivism and metacognitive.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cognition、cognitive、cognitively、cognitivism 与 metacognitive。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: cognitive development, cognitive science, cognitive bias, cognitive load.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：认知发展、认知科学、认知偏差、认知负荷。

normal.en: Cognitive describes the domain, not the quality; a cognitive bias can be irrational.
normal.cn: cognitive 描述领域，而非质量；认知偏差可以是不理性的。

normal.en: The adverb cognitively usually modifies verbs such as process, assess or decline.
normal.cn: 副词形式通常修饰「加工、评估、衰退」这类动词。

abstract.en: Picture a map with three marked stops: see, store, infer.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图标出三站：看、存、推。

abstract.en: Picture a workbench where raw sensory material is turned into a finished judgment.
abstract.cn: 想象一张工作台，把感官原料加工成判断成品。

abstract.en: Picture a light that falls only on the thinking half of a face.
abstract.cn: 想象一束光只照在脸孔中「思考」的那一半。

examples.en: Cognitive development is fastest in the first years of life.
examples.cn: 认知发展在生命最初几年最快。

examples.en: The test measures cognitive flexibility rather than factual recall.
examples.cn: 这项测验衡量认知灵活性，而非事实记忆。

examples.en: Cognitive therapy helped her question the belief that she was failing.
examples.cn: 认知疗法帮助她质疑自己正在失败这一信念。

dict_mnemonic.text: cognition（认知）+ ive（……的）——属于认知活动的 → 认知的

root: 晚期拉丁 cognitivus「有认识能力的」← cognit-（cognoscere「得知」的分词词干）+ -ivus；与 cognition 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses show the adjective attaching itself to tasks, to a discipline, to development, to named failure modes, to a school, to a therapy, to a field and to a slice of meaning.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项显示这个形容词依次贴到任务、学科、发展、有名的失败模式、学派、疗法、领域，以及意义的一个切面上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tag marked 'knowing' pinned onto one item after another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚写着「知」的标签，被钉到一个又一个事物上。

branches.en: THE DOMAIN: the adjective first marks the mental territory and the discipline that owns it.
branches.cn: 领域：这个形容词先标出心智领地，以及拥有这片领地的学科。

branches.en: TIME: development adds a growing line to the same territory.
branches.cn: 时间：发展给同一片领地加上一条生长的线。

branches.en: FAILURE MODES: bias and load are the named ways the machinery strains.
branches.cn: 失败模式：偏差与负荷是这台机器吃力时被命名的样子。

branches.en: APPLICATIONS: a linguistic school and a therapy both claim the adjective as their base.
branches.cn: 应用：一个语言学派与一种疗法都把这个形容词当作自己的根基。

branches.en: INSTITUTION AND MEANING: the adjective labels an interdisciplinary field and the denotative half of a word.
branches.cn: 建制与意义：这个形容词既标出一个交叉学科，也标出词语意义中「指物」的一半。

intro.en: Cognitive is a Latin participle stem plus the adjective suffix -ive; it has no independent prefix of its own, since com- is already inside the stem.
intro.cn: cognitive 是拉丁分词词干加形容词后缀 -ive；它本身没有独立前缀，因为 com- 已经含在词干里。

latinIntro.en: Cognoscere 'to get to know' yields cognit- and cognitivus; English adds cognition, cognitive, cognitively and the modern compound metacognitive.
latinIntro.cn: cognoscere「得知」生成 cognit- 与 cognitivus；英语再加上 cognition、cognitive、cognitively 与现代复合词 metacognitive。

items.example: The stem carries the finished act of knowing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载已完成的「知」。

items.meaning: tending to, having the nature of
items.example: The suffix turns the stem into a descriptive adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词干变成描述性形容词。

items.example: Cognitive tasks test more than memory.
items.exampleCN: 认知任务测验的不止记忆。

items.meaning: the act or faculty of knowing
items.example: Cognition is the noun behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: cognition 是形容词背后的名词。

items.example: The patient remained cognitively intact.
items.exampleCN: 病人在认知上保持完好。

items.meaning: the view that mind is information processing
items.meaningCN: 认为心智是信息加工的观点
items.example: Cognitivism dominated psychology in the 1970s.
items.exampleCN: 认知主义在 20 世纪 70 年代主导心理学。

items.example: A cognitivist treats beliefs as representations.
items.exampleCN: 认知主义者把信念当作表征。

items.meaning: relating to thinking about one's own thinking
items.meaningCN: 元认知的；对自己的思考进行思考的
items.example: Metacognitive strategies help students monitor themselves.
items.exampleCN: 元认知策略帮助学生监控自己。

items.example: Cognoscere is the ultimate source of the family.
items.exampleCN: cognoscere 是整个词族的最终来源。

definition_zh: v. 连贯，一致；（物质）黏合，附着
definition_en: to be logically connected and easy to follow; to stick together as one mass
core_image: 一段话的句子像扣在一起的链条
scene: 一篇好文章必须前后连贯，读者才跟得上。A good essay must cohere so that the reader can follow.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：cohere 指逻辑连贯；句意是一篇好文章必须前后连贯，读者才跟得上。

senses.title: To be logically connected
senses.definition: to fit together so that the parts make sense as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 各部分配合成为有意义的整体
senses.example: The argument does not cohere.
senses.exampleCN: 这个论证前后不连贯。
senses.why: Latin co means together and haerere means to stick.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 co 意为一起，haerere 意为黏附。

senses.title: To stick together physically
senses.definition: to hold together as a solid mass
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体黏在一起
senses.example: The particles cohere into a solid mass.
senses.exampleCN: 颗粒黏结成一块固体。
senses.why: The physical sense is the older one.
senses.whyCN: 物理黏合义更古老。

intro.en: Cohere is literally to stick together, then to make sense together.
intro.cn: cohere 字面是黏在一起，引申为前后说得通。

items.en: Co means together.
items.cn: co 意为一起。

items.en: Haerere means to stick or cling.
items.cn: haerere 意为黏附、附着。

items.en: Cohere enters English as a verb of sticking.
items.cn: 十六世纪 cohere 作为黏附动词进入英语。

items.en: Writers use it for arguments that hold together.
items.cn: 十七世纪作家用它形容论证自洽。

items.en: Particles are said to cohere.
items.cn: 现代物理学说颗粒黏结。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the coher- shape; the near-meaning group names sticking and fitting.
note.cn: 形近组共享 coher- 词形；近义组列出黏附与契合。

entries.definition: Clear and logically connected.
entries.definitionCN: 连贯的。

entries.definition: The state of sticking together.
entries.definitionCN: 凝聚力。

entries.definition: In or to this place.
entries.definitionCN: 这里。

entries.definition: To join one thing to another.
entries.definitionCN: 连接。

entries.definition: To stick firmly to a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 黏附。

entries.definition: To be in harmony with something.
entries.definitionCN: 一致。

normalIntro.en: Cohere means the parts stick to each other.
normalIntro.cn: cohere 就是各部分互相黏住。

normal.en: Co means together.
normal.cn: co 意为一起。

normal.en: Haerere means stick.
normal.cn: haerere 意为黏。

normal.en: Glue makes paper cohere.
normal.cn: 胶水让纸黏合。

normal.en: Good paragraphs cohere.
normal.cn: 好段落前后连贯。

normal.en: Coherent writing holds together.
normal.cn: 连贯的文章是一体的。

abstract.en: A chain made of sentences.
abstract.cn: 由句子做成的链。

abstract.en: Sand learning to be stone.
abstract.cn: 学会成为石头的沙。

abstract.en: Ideas holding hands.
abstract.cn: 互相牵手的观点。

examples.en: The chapters cohere around a single theme.
examples.cn: 各章围绕一个主题前后连贯。

examples.en: Wet clay coheres into a ball.
examples.cn: 湿黏土黏成一个球。

examples.en: His account does not cohere with the facts.
examples.cn: 他的说法与事实不一致。

dict_mnemonic.text: co（一起）+ here（黏）→ 黏在一起，即连贯、黏合。

root: 拉丁 co（一起）+ haerere（黏附）→ 拉丁 cohaerere → 英语 cohere

sensesIntro.en: Things that stick together, and ideas that hold together, share one verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 黏在一起的东西与说得通的观点共用一个动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two surfaces joined with no gap between
core.cn: 核心意象：两面之间几乎没有缝隙的黏合

branches.en: Clay pressed into one ball.
branches.cn: 被按成一团的黏土。

branches.en: Particles forming a solid.
branches.cn: 结成固体的颗粒。

branches.en: A paragraph with a clear thread.
branches.cn: 线索清晰的段落。

branches.en: An argument that matches the facts.
branches.cn: 与事实相符的论证。

branches.en: Sticking in matter and in meaning.
