definition_zh: 连贯的；前后一致的；黏合在一起的；相干的
definition_en: sticking together so that the parts form a connected, consistent whole
core_image: 许多散块被黏成一体，抽掉哪一块，整体就散架
scene: 这组词中，An editor taps a paragraph and says: This paragraph is clear, but the essay as a whole is not coherent yet.
sceneCN: 这里 coherent 是「（文章整体）连贯的、前后一致的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这一段本身清楚，但整篇文章还不够连贯。画面里是红笔、稿件和贴满便签的墙。

senses.title: Text: parts joined so the meaning flows
senses.titleCN: 连贯的：各部分接上，意思能流动
senses.definition: of speech or writing, logically connected and easy to follow
senses.definitionCN: （口语或文章）逻辑连接、容易跟上的
senses.example: Her essay is coherent from the first paragraph to the last.
senses.exampleCN: 她的文章从第一段到最后一段都很连贯。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to stick together'. Sentences cohere when each one sticks to the next, so the reader can walk across the paragraph without a gap.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词本义是“黏在一起”。句子彼此黏住，读者就能走过整段而没有断口，这就是连贯。

senses.title: Argument: claims that hold each other up
senses.definition: of ideas or an argument, consistent with one another and forming a single case
senses.definitionCN: （观点或论证）彼此一致，构成一个整体主张
senses.example: The theory is coherent: every claim supports the next.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论前后一致：每个主张都支撑下一个。
senses.why: Sticking together is not mere sequence but mutual support. In an argument each claim must adhere to the others, or the structure pulls apart when one is pressed.
senses.whyCN: 黏在一起不只是排成顺序，而是互相支撑。在论证里，每个主张都得附着在别的主张上，否则一压就散。

senses.title: Person: a mind whose words still connect
senses.titleCN: 表达清楚的：话还连得起来的人
senses.definition: of a person, able to think and speak in a clear, connected way
senses.definitionCN: （人）能够清楚、有条理地思考和表达的
senses.example: The patient was drowsy but coherent after the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术之后病人昏昏欲睡，但说话还有条理。
senses.why: When the mind holds together, its output holds together. A coherent patient is one whose thoughts still stick to one another, which is why doctors test coherence after sedation.
senses.whyCN: 思维黏得住，说出的话就黏得住。coherent 的病人是思想仍彼此相连的人，所以医生在麻醉后要测试“连贯性”。

senses.title: Waves: crests that keep the same step
senses.titleCN: 相干的：波峰始终踩着同一步点
senses.definition: of waves, having the same frequency and a constant phase difference, so they can interfere stably
senses.definitionCN: （波）频率相同、相位差恒定，因而能稳定干涉的
senses.example: Two coherent beams produce a stable interference pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 两束相干光产生稳定的干涉图样。
senses.why: Physics took the 'sticking together' image literally: wave crests that stay locked in step remain glued to one another over distance, so their pattern does not blur.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把这个“黏在一起”的意象照字面用了：波峰始终同步，就在长距离上彼此黏住，图样因此不会糊掉。

senses.title: Group: many wills acting as one body
senses.titleCN: 协调一致的：众多意志像一个身体那样行动
senses.definition: of a group or policy, united and consistent so that the parts do not work against each other
senses.definitionCN: （群体或政策）统一而一致，各部分不相互抵触
senses.example: The party needs a coherent policy on housing.
senses.exampleCN: 这个党需要一套协调一致的住房政策。
senses.why: A group is coherent when its members stick to one line. The physical image of parts adhering becomes social: no faction pulls away from the whole.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体在成员都黏在一条线上时才是连贯的。部分附着的物理意象变成社会意象：没有哪一派从整体上扯开。

senses.title: Substance: a mass that holds its shape
senses.titleCN: 黏合的：能保持形状的一团物质
senses.definition: of a material, sticking together firmly as a single mass
senses.definitionCN: （材料）牢固地黏成一团
senses.example: The wet clay stayed coherent enough to be shaped by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 湿黏土黏得足够结实，可以用手塑形。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense: particles that adhere to one another form a coherent mass. Everything abstract later borrows this picture of a body that does not crumble.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的物理义：相互附着的颗粒形成一团黏合的物质。后来一切抽象用法都借用了这个“不散架的身体”的图景。

senses.title: Laser light: one wavelength in lockstep
senses.titleCN: 相干光：步调一致的一束光
senses.definition: of light, having a single wavelength and a fixed phase relationship, as in a laser
senses.definitionCN: （光）波长单一、相位关系固定，如激光
senses.example: A coherent beam can carry a signal across a room without spreading.
senses.exampleCN: 相干光束能把信号送过房间而不发散。
senses.why: Ordinary light is a crowd of waves out of step; laser light is a column marching in step. Coherent here means the waves are so glued in rhythm that the beam stays narrow.
senses.whyCN: 普通光是步调杂乱的一群波；激光是齐步走的一列。这里的 coherent 指波在节奏上黏得如此紧，光束因此保持狭窄。

senses.title: Account: a story with no missing joints
senses.titleCN: 条理清楚的：关节齐全的叙述
senses.definition: of an account or explanation, orderly and intelligible, with no gaps in the sequence
senses.definitionCN: （叙述或解释）有条理、可理解，顺序上没有缺环
senses.example: He gave a coherent account of what happened that night.
senses.exampleCN: 他对那晚发生的事做了条理清楚的叙述。
senses.why: A story coheres when cause sticks to effect and each scene sticks to the next. Where a joint is missing, the listener feels the seam, and we say the account is incoherent.
senses.whyCN: 当因黏住果、每一幕黏住下一幕时，故事就连贯。缺一个关节，听者就摸到接缝，我们便说叙述不连贯。

senses.title: Strategy: a plan whose pieces agree
senses.titleCN: 成体系的：各块彼此呼应的计划
senses.definition: of a plan or set of actions, internally consistent and aimed at one goal
senses.definitionCN: （计划或行动组合）内部一致、指向同一目标
senses.example: The company lacks a coherent strategy for its overseas branches.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司对其海外分支机构缺乏一套连贯的战略。
senses.why: A strategy is coherent when its decisions stick to one aim; if each department pulls in its own direction, the plan has no single body to hold it together.
senses.whyCN: 当各项决策都黏在同一个目标上，战略才连贯；若每个部门各自拉扯，计划就没有一个整体来维持它。

intro.en: Coherent comes from Latin cohaerere, 'to stick together'. The physical sense of parts adhering is the source of every later sense: text, argument, group, mind and light all 'hold together'.
intro.cn: coherent 来自拉丁语 cohaerere“黏在一起”。部分附着的物理义是后来一切义项的源头：文章、论证、群体、心智、光，全都“黏得住”。

items.en: Cohaerere meant 'to stick together, be connected'. It was com- 'together' plus haerere 'to adhere, stick, cling'.
items.cn: cohaerere 意为“黏在一起、相连”，由 com-“一起”加 haerere“附着、黏住、紧贴”构成。

items.en: The adjective enters English as 'harmonious', a sense close to the Latin participle: things that fit and hold together without conflict.
items.cn: 该形容词以“和谐的”义进入英语，接近拉丁分词的意思：彼此贴合、黏在一起而不冲突。

items.en: By the 1570s it also meant 'sticking together' physically, and 'connected, consistent' of speech and thought.
items.cn: 到 1570 年代，它也表示物理上的“黏在一起”，以及言语和思想上的“连贯、一致”。

items.en: Optics and later physics adopted coherence for waves that keep a fixed phase relationship; a coherent beam is literally a set of waves marching in step.
items.cn: 光学及后来的物理学采用 coherence 指保持固定相位关系的波；相干光束字面上就是齐步走的一组波。

items.en: Modern usage extends the word to persons ('coherent after the accident'), to organizations and to policy, always asking whether the parts still hold together.
items.cn: 现代用法把该词扩展到人（“事故后神志清楚”）、组织与政策，问的始终是：各部分是否还黏得住。

items.en: Haerere itself is of uncertain origin. Watkins proposed PIE *ghais- 'to adhere', but some linguists reject the link and de Vaan offers no etymology, so the deepest step is source uncertain.
items.cn: haerere 本身来源不确定。Watkins 提出原始印欧语 *ghais-“附着”，但一些语言学家否定这一联系，de Vaan 也未给出词源，故最深层来源不确定。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: to stick together or be logically connected. It is the verb behind coherent.
entries.definitionCN: 黏合；连贯一致。它是 coherent 背后的动词。

entries.definition: the quality of being connected and consistent. It is the noun of coherent.
entries.definitionCN: 连贯性；一致性。它是 coherent 的名词。

entries.definition: not connected or not able to speak clearly. It is in- 'not' plus coherent.
entries.definitionCN: 不连贯的；语无伦次的。它是 in-“不”加 coherent。

entries.definition: sticking to a surface, or a supporter of a cause. It shares the Latin root haerere 'to stick'.
entries.definitionCN: 附着的；拥护者。它与 coherent 同出拉丁词根 haerere“黏住”。

entries.definition: always behaving or being stated in the same way. It stresses agreement over time rather than physical joining.
entries.definitionCN: 一致的；始终如一的。它强调时间上的相符，而非物理连接。

entries.definition: following clear rules of reasoning. It focuses on inference, while coherent focuses on the whole holding together.
entries.definitionCN: 合乎逻辑的。它聚焦推理规则，而 coherent 聚焦整体是否黏得住。

entries.definition: forming a united whole; tending to stick together. It is close to the physical and social senses of coherent.
entries.definitionCN: 有凝聚力的；黏合的。它接近 coherent 的物理义与社会义。

entries.definition: made into a single whole. It describes the result, where coherent describes the holding-together.
entries.definitionCN: 统一的；一体化的。它描述结果，而 coherent 描述黏合的状态。

entries.definition: expressed clearly and easy to understand. It matches the clarity of a coherent explanation but not its structure.
entries.definitionCN: 清晰易懂的。它对应连贯解释的清晰，但不涉及结构。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin com- and haerere, the cohere family, and the derived forms English actually uses.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 com- 与 haerere、cohere 词族，以及英语实际使用的派生形式。

normal.en: coherent = co- 'together' + haerere 'to stick': the parts are glued, so the whole holds.
normal.cn: coherent = co-“一起”+ haerere“黏”：各部分被黏住，整体才立得住。

normal.en: The same haerere gives adhere, adherent and adhesion: all about one thing clinging to another.
normal.cn: 同一个 haerere 还给出 adhere、adherent、adhesion：都是关于一物紧贴另一物。

normal.en: coherence is what an essay, a policy and a laser beam can all have: the pieces keep the same step.
normal.cn: coherence 是文章、政策和激光束都能有的东西：各块保持同一步点。

normal.en: incoherent is in- 'not' + coherent: words that will not stick, so a drunk or a feverish person becomes incoherent.
normal.cn: incoherent 是 in-“不”+ coherent：话黏不起来，所以醉酒或发烧的人会语无伦次。

normal.en: Doctors ask a patient to count backwards to test whether the mind is still coherent.
normal.cn: 医生让病人倒着数数，就是测试他的思维是否还连贯。

abstract.en: The core operation is adhesion: separate pieces must grip one another before anything larger can exist.
abstract.cn: 核心动作是黏附：分开的块必须先互相咬住，更大的东西才可能存在。

abstract.en: The same grip is scaled to sentences, arguments, groups, minds and waves; in each case the test is whether a piece can be pulled away.
abstract.cn: 同一种咬合被缩放到句子、论证、群体、心智和波；每一次的检验都是：能否把某一块抽走。

abstract.en: So 'logical', 'consistent', 'unified' and 'in step' are not separate meanings but one question: does the whole still hold when pressed?
abstract.cn: 所以“合乎逻辑、前后一致、统一、同步”并非彼此无关，而是同一个问题：受压时整体还立得住吗？

examples.en: She gave a clear and coherent explanation of the new rules.
examples.cn: 她对新规则做了清楚而连贯的解释。

examples.en: The government has failed to produce a coherent energy policy.
examples.cn: 政府未能拿出一套协调一致的能源政策。

examples.en: The witness was too shaken to give a coherent account.
examples.cn: 那名证人受惊过度，无法做出条理清楚的叙述。

dict_mnemonic.text: co（一起）+ here（这里）+ ent——把所有材料都“一起放在这里”黏住 → coherent 连贯的

root: 源自拉丁语 cohaerere“黏在一起”，由 com-“一起”+ haerere“附着、黏住”构成，核心是“各部分黏成一体”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of coherent, all traced to one act: parts sticking together. Sentences, claims, minds, waves, groups, clay, laser light, stories and strategies are all tested by whether their pieces still hold.
sensesIntro.cn: coherent 的九个义项都追溯到一个动作：各部分黏在一起。句子、主张、心智、波、群体、黏土、激光、故事与战略，检验的都是各块是否还黏得住。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate pieces adhering into one body that does not fall apart.
core.cn: 核心意象：分开的块黏附成一个不散架的整体。

branches.en: WORDS STICK: sentences joined into a flowing text, and events joined into an intelligible account.
branches.cn: 词句黏合：句子接成流动的文章，事件接成可理解的叙述。

branches.en: CLAIMS STICK: an argument whose claims support one another, and a strategy whose decisions serve one aim.
branches.cn: 主张黏合：论点彼此支撑的论证，以及决策服务同一目标的战略。

branches.en: THE MIND STICKS: a person whose thoughts still connect, the medical test of coherence.
branches.cn: 心智黏合：思想仍能相连的人，也就是医学上的连贯性测试。

branches.en: WAVES STICK: crests locked in phase, from interference patterns to a laser beam that does not spread.
branches.cn: 波黏合：波峰锁在同一相位，从干涉图样到不发散的激光束。

branches.en: BODIES STICK: clay that holds its shape, and a group whose members hold one line.
branches.cn: 形体黏合：保持形状的黏土，以及成员守同一条线的群体。

intro.en: Coherent is co- + haerere + -ent. Its family shows the prefix com-/co-, the root haer- 'stick', and the suffixes -ent, -ence, -sion and -ive.
intro.cn: coherent 是 co- + haerere + -ent。它的词族展示了前缀 com-/co-、词根 haer-“黏”，以及后缀 -ent、-ence、-sion、-ive。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb cohaerere 'to stick together' yields coherent, coherence and cohere. Its participle haesus gives cohesion, while adhaerere gives adhere and adherent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 cohaerere“黏在一起”给出 coherent、coherence、cohere。它的分词 haesus 给出 cohesion，而 adhaerere 给出 adhere 与 adherent。

items.meaningCN: 连贯的；一致的；黏合的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.example: The report is coherent and well argued.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告连贯且论证充分。

items.meaningCN: 连贯地；有条理地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: He could not speak coherently after the fall.
items.exampleCN: 摔倒后他说话语无伦次。

items.meaning: the state of sticking together or being consistent
items.meaningCN: 连贯性；一致性；相干性（-ence 构成名词）
items.example: The essay lacks coherence between paragraphs.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章段与段之间缺乏连贯。

items.meaning: not connected; unable to speak clearly
items.meaningCN: 不连贯的；语无伦次的（in- 表否定）
items.example: He was incoherent with pain.
items.exampleCN: 他痛得语无伦次。

items.meaningCN: 不连贯；语无伦次（in- 表否定）
items.example: The incoherence of the plan worried investors.
items.exampleCN: 计划的不连贯让投资者担忧。

items.meaning: to stick together or be logically consistent
items.meaningCN: 黏合；连贯一致（动词原形）
items.example: The chapters cohere into a single story.
items.exampleCN: 这些章节黏合成一个完整的故事。

items.meaning: the act or state of sticking together; unity
items.meaningCN: 黏合；凝聚力（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: Sport builds cohesion within a team.
items.exampleCN: 运动能建立团队内部的凝聚力。

items.meaning: to stick fast to a surface or follow a rule closely
items.example: The tape adheres to damp surfaces.
items.exampleCN: 这种胶带能粘在潮湿表面。

items.meaning: sticking to something; a supporter of a cause
items.meaningCN: 附着的；拥护者（-ent 表人或形容词）
items.example: He is a loyal adherent of the old theory.
items.exampleCN: 他是旧理论的忠实拥护者。

items.meaning: to exist as a natural quality in something
items.example: Risk inheres in every investment.
items.exampleCN: 每一项投资都固有风险。

definition_zh: 黏合力；凝聚力；（语言学）篇章衔接；（群体）团结
definition_en: the force or quality by which parts stick together, whether molecules, group members or sentences
core_image: 细管里的水柱被自己内部的力量拉住，高出杯口也不落下
scene: 把细管插进水里，水柱自己爬了上来，高出杯口却不肯落下。Water climbs the narrow tube because cohesion holds the molecules together.
sceneCN: 这里 cohesion 指物质内部分子彼此黏合的力量（第 1 个义项：物理黏合力）；句意为水能爬上细管，是因为黏合力把分子拉在一起。

pos.zh: 黏合力；凝聚力（不可数，指黏合的状态或力量）
（语言学）衔接（不可数，指篇章内部的连接关系）

derivatives.zh: 黏合；连贯（由拉丁 cohaerere「黏在一起」进入，核心是「彼此附着」，是本词的基础动词）
有黏合力的；有凝聚力的（由「凝聚力」一词的形容词形式而来，由状态转指性质）
连贯的；一致的（由拉丁词根加表共同的前缀，构成另一形容词形式，由「粘住」转指「说得通」）
连贯性（由基础形容词加表状态的名词后缀而来，由性质转指状态，常与 cohesion 对照）
黏附（由拉丁词根加表朝向的前缀而来，由「黏住」转为「附着到别的表面」）

senses.title: Physical sticking
senses.definition: the attraction that holds molecules of the same substance together
senses.definitionCN: 把同种物质的分子拉在一起的那种吸引力
senses.example: Cohesion pulls the water into a rounded drop on the leaf.
senses.exampleCN: 黏合力把水在叶面上拉成一颗圆润的水珠。
senses.why: The oldest sense is literal: things of one kind cling to one another, as water molecules do.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是字面的：同类之物彼此附着，就像水分子那样。

senses.title: Social unity
senses.definition: the strength of the bonds that keep a community or society together
senses.definitionCN: 使一个共同体或社会保持一体的纽带强度
senses.example: Cohesion in the village survived the closure of the mine.
senses.exampleCN: 矿井关闭之后，村子里的凝聚力仍然存在。
senses.why: The physical image transfers to people: what holds molecules together becomes what holds neighbours together.
senses.whyCN: 物理意象被移用到人身上：把分子拉住的力量，变成把邻里拉住的力量。

senses.title: Group and team cohesion
senses.definition: the degree to which members of a group are attached to it and to one another
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体的成员对群体及彼此依附的程度
senses.example: The coach measured cohesion before the final match.
senses.exampleCN: 教练在决赛前测量了团队凝聚力。
senses.why: Psychology made cohesion a variable: something a group can have more or less of, and something that can be built.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把凝聚力变成变量：一个群体可以多一点或少一点，也可以被刻意建设。

senses.title: Textual cohesion
senses.definition: the ties of reference, substitution and conjunction that make a text hold together
senses.definitionCN: 由照应、替代与连接构成、使篇章连成一体的各种联系
senses.example: Cohesion in the paragraph comes from repeated pronouns and linkers.
senses.exampleCN: 这一段的衔接来自重复出现的代词与连接词。
senses.why: Linguists borrowed the word for the surface links between sentences: text also has a kind of glue.
senses.whyCN: 语言学者借用了这个词来表示句子之间的表面连接：文本也有一种黏合剂。

senses.title: Cohesive devices
senses.definition: the specific words and structures, such as pronouns and ellipsis, that create those ties
senses.definitionCN: 造成这些联系的具体词与结构，如代词与省略
senses.example: The essay lists cohesion devices before it asks students to write.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章先列出衔接手段，再让学生动笔。
senses.why: Once the concept exists, it can be broken into parts that teachers can name and test.
senses.whyCN: 概念一旦存在，就能被拆成教师可以命名与检测的部件。

senses.title: Cohesion versus coherence
senses.definition: the difference between surface links and the underlying sense that a text makes
senses.definitionCN: 表面连接与文本整体说得通这层意思之间的区别
senses.example: The paragraph has cohesion but no coherence: the links lead nowhere.
senses.exampleCN: 这段有衔接却没有连贯：连接词通向不了任何地方。
senses.why: Glue is not meaning; a text can be tightly linked and still say nothing, so the pair must be distinguished.
senses.whyCN: 胶水不等于意义；文本可以连接紧密却什么也没说，因此必须区分这两个概念。

senses.title: Alliance cohesion
senses.definition: the willingness of partners or coalition members to stay together under disagreement
senses.definitionCN: 伙伴或联盟成员在分歧之下仍愿意留在一起的程度
senses.example: Cohesion among the allies weakened when the funding ended.
senses.exampleCN: 资金终止后，盟友之间的凝聚力削弱了。
senses.why: Politics applies the word to agreements between bodies, where unity is tested by competing interests.
senses.whyCN: 政治把这个词用到团体间的协议上，其团结受到彼此竞争的利益的检验。

senses.title: A measured target
senses.definition: an index or policy aim expressing how united a group or society should be
senses.definitionCN: 表达一个群体或社会应有多团结的指数或政策目标
senses.example: The programme reports cohesion as a score for each district.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目把凝聚力作为每个城区的分数来报告。
senses.why: Measurement turns a bond into a number, and a number can become a target to be managed.
senses.whyCN: 测量把纽带变成数字，而数字可以变成被管理的目标。

intro.en: Cohesion comes from Latin cohaesus, the past participle of cohaerere 'to stick together', built on com- 'together' and haerere 'to cling'. English borrowed the noun in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cohesion 来自拉丁 cohaesus，即 cohaerere「黏在一起」的过去分词，由表示「共同」的前缀加 haerere「附着」构成。英语在十七世纪借入这个名词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Haerere meant 'to stick, cling, be fixed'. It also lies behind adhere and hesitation, where being stuck turns into a pause.
items.cn: haerere 意为「黏住、附着、固定」。它也是 adhere 与 hesitation 的来源，其中「被粘住」转成了「停顿」。

items.en: Cohaerere added com- 'together' to haerere, giving 'to stick together, be connected'. Its participle is cohaesus.
items.cn: cohaerere 在 haerere 前加表示「共同」的前缀，得到「黏在一起、相互连接」。其分词是 cohaesus。

items.en: The noun cohaesio named the state of being stuck together; it could describe both bodies and arguments.
items.cn: 名词 cohaesio 命名黏在一起的状态，既能描述物体，也能描述论证。

items.en: English cohesion appears in the seventeenth century, first in physical and philosophical writing, then in social description.
items.cn: 英语 cohesion 在十七世纪出现，先见于物理与哲学写作，后进入社会描述。

items.en: Halliday and Hasan made cohesion a central term of text linguistics in 1976, listing reference, substitution, ellipsis, conjunction and lexical ties.
items.cn: 韩礼德与哈桑在一九七六年把 cohesion 变成篇章语言学的核心术语，列出照应、替代、省略、连接与词汇衔接。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of haerere is not established, and the exact date of the English noun's first use varies between dictionaries.
items.cn: 来源不确定：haerere 在拉丁语之前的来源未得到证明；这个英语名词首次使用的确切年代，各词典说法不一。

note.en: Group one separates words built on the same stick root; group two holds terms for unity and connection.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一「黏住」词根的词；第二组是团结与连接的术语。

entries.definition: Logical consistency, especially of an argument or text; it is about intelligibility, not glue.
entries.definitionCN: 逻辑上的一致性，尤指论证或文本；它关乎可理解性，而非黏合。

entries.definition: Attachment of one substance to a different surface; the prefix means 'to', not 'together'.
entries.definitionCN: 一种物质附着到另一种表面；前缀意为「朝向」，而非「共同」。

entries.definition: Holding together; it describes the quality, while cohesion names the state or force.
entries.definitionCN: 有黏合力的；形容词描述性质，cohesion 命名状态或力量。

entries.definition: To hold together or be consistent; it names the process that cohesion results from.
entries.definitionCN: 黏合；前后一致。它命名产生凝聚力的过程。

entries.definition: Active support among people with shared interests; it is cohesion in action.
entries.definitionCN: 有共同利益者之间的主动支持；它是行动中的凝聚力。

entries.definition: The state of being one whole; it is broader and less mechanical than cohesion.
entries.definitionCN: 成为一个整体的状态；比凝聚力更宽，也更少机械意味。

entries.definition: The process of combining parts into one system; cohesion is the resulting hold, integration is the making.
entries.definitionCN: 把部分合成一个系统的过程；凝聚力是结果性的黏合，整合是制造过程。

entries.definition: Agreement of parts with one standard over time; it concerns regularity rather than sticking.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分长期符合同一标准；它关乎规律性，而非黏合。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb, its real relatives and real technical uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、其真实同族词与真实的技术用法。

normal.en: Cohesion is sticking together; adhesion is sticking to something else.
normal.cn: cohesion 是黏在一起；adhesion 是黏到别的东西上。

normal.en: The family runs cohere, cohesion, cohesive, coherent, coherence.
normal.cn: 词族包括 cohere、cohesion、cohesive、coherent、coherence。

normal.en: Cohesion is glue, coherence is sense: a text can have one without the other.
normal.cn: cohesion 是胶水，coherence 是意义：文本可以有其一而无其二。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the range: social cohesion, group cohesion, cohesion and coherence, molecular cohesion.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出范围：社会凝聚力、群体凝聚力、衔接与连贯、分子黏合力。

normal.en: The noun is uncountable: more cohesion, less cohesion, never 'cohesions'.
normal.cn: 这个名词不可数：凝聚力多一些、少一些，不说「几个凝聚力」。

abstract.en: Picture water rising in a narrow tube because it holds on to itself.
abstract.cn: 想象水在细管里上升，因为它拉住了自己。

abstract.en: Picture a paragraph whose pronouns all point back to one another and to nothing else.
abstract.cn: 想象一段文字，所有代词都指回彼此，却不指向任何别的什么。

abstract.en: Picture an alliance held together only by the funding that is about to end.
abstract.cn: 想象一个联盟，只靠那笔即将终止的资金维系。

examples.en: Surface tension and cohesion explain why the insect can walk on water.
examples.cn: 表面张力与黏合力解释了昆虫为何能在水面上行走。

examples.en: The teacher marked cohesion separately from argument.
examples.cn: 老师把衔接与论证分开评分。

examples.en: Economic shock can destroy the cohesion of a small town in a single year.
examples.cn: 经济冲击能在一年之内摧毁一个小镇的凝聚力。

dict_mnemonic.text: co-（共同）+ haerere（黏住）+ -sion（状态）＝ 彼此黏住的状态；记「水爬细管，字连成段」。

root: 源自拉丁 cohaerere「黏在一起」的过去分词 cohaesus，再由名词 cohaesio 进入英语；该动词由前缀表「共同」加 haerere「附着」构成，haerere 更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from molecular attraction to social unity, team psychology, textual ties, cohesive devices, the contrast with coherence, alliance politics and measured targets.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从分子吸引，移到社会团结、团队心理、篇章联系、衔接手段、与连贯的对照、联盟政治与被测量的目标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water holding itself up inside a narrow tube.
core.cn: 核心意象：水在细管里把自己托住。

branches.en: MOLECULES: the literal attraction of like to like.
branches.cn: 分子：同类相吸的字面力量。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND PARTNERS: neighbours held together, and allies held through disagreement.
branches.cn: 邻里与伙伴：被拉住邻里，以及在分歧中仍被拉住的盟友。

branches.en: THE TEAM: cohesion becomes a variable a coach can build and measure.
branches.cn: 团队：凝聚力变成教练可以建设与测量的变量。

branches.en: THE TEXT: surface links between sentences, then the named devices that create them.
branches.cn: 文本：句子之间的表面连接，再是造成这些连接的具名手段。

branches.en: GLUE VERSUS SENSE, AND THE SCORE: links without meaning, and a bond turned into a number.
branches.cn: 胶水与意义，以及分数：没有意义的连接，和被变成数字的纽带。

intro.en: Cohesion is a Latin noun of sticking; its stem builds a compact family of verbs, adjectives and nouns.
intro.cn: cohesion 是表示「黏合」的拉丁名词；其词干构成一个紧凑的动词、形容词与名词词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin com- and haerere, through cohaerere and cohaesus, supply every morpheme. The related ad- form gives adhesion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁表示「共同」的前缀与 haerere，经 cohaerere 与 cohaesus，提供全部语素。相关的表示「朝向」的形式给出 adhesion。

items.example: The chapters cohere around one question.
items.exampleCN: 各章围绕一个问题连成一体。

items.example: Cohesion depends on shared rituals.
items.exampleCN: 凝聚力依赖共享仪式。

items.example: The group remained cohesive under pressure.
items.exampleCN: 这个群体在压力下仍保持凝聚。

items.example: She gave a coherent account of the night.
items.exampleCN: 她对那晚作了连贯的陈述。

items.example: The essay lacks coherence after page three.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章从第三页起就缺乏连贯。

items.meaning: to stick to; to follow a rule
items.example: Members adhere to the same code.
items.exampleCN: 成员遵守同一套准则。

items.example: Adhesion failed in the damp air.
items.exampleCN: 在潮湿空气中黏附失效了。

items.example: He answered without hesitation.
items.exampleCN: 他毫不犹豫地回答。

definition_zh: 铸币；硬币制度；新造的词（或新造之物）；铸币权
definition_en: the system of coins used in a country, the act of making them, or a newly invented word
core_image: 一枚银片夹在两块模具之间，锤子落下，花纹从边缘挤进银面
scene: 作坊里，工匠把一枚银片放在两片模具之间，用锤子砸下，边缘的花纹陷进银面。The coinage of the realm changed when the old die wore out.
sceneCN: 这里 coinage 指「一国所使用的硬币体系」（第 1 个义项：作为整套流通硬币）；句意为旧模具磨损之后，这个王国的铸币体系随之改变。

pos.zh: 铸币；硬币体系；新造词（不可数，或作可数指一种币制）

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 cuneus（楔子）经古法语 coin（模具）→ 硬币；铸造；造词
coin + -er（从事者）→ 铸币者；造词者（语义偏移：从工人转到造词人）
coin + -ing（动名词）→ 铸造；造词行为
coin + operated → 投币式的（语义偏移：从货币转到机械）
mint + -age（同型后缀，不同词干）→ 铸造量；铸币费
neo-（新）+ logos（词）→ 新词（同义不同源）

senses.title: The coins of a country as a system
senses.titleCN: 一国硬币构成的整套体系
senses.definition: the set of coins in use in a country, considered as one system with fixed denominations
senses.definitionCN: 一国流通中按固定面额组成的整套硬币
senses.example: The coinage of the realm changed when the old die wore out.
senses.exampleCN: 旧模具磨损之后，这个王国的铸币体系随之改变。
senses.why: The Latin word for a wedge named the die that stamped metal, and the product took the name of the tool.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中表「楔子」的词指冲压金属的模具，产物便继承了工具之名。

senses.title: The act or process of minting
senses.definition: the work of cutting dies and striking blanks into legal coins
senses.definitionCN: 刻制模具并把坯饼冲压成法定硬币的工作
senses.example: Coinage was moved to the capital so the dies could be guarded.
senses.exampleCN: 铸币工序迁到首都，以便看守模具。
senses.why: The suffix -age names an action or its product, so the same noun covers the making and the made.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -age 既指动作也指产物，因此同一个名词兼指制造与制成品。

senses.title: A newly invented word
senses.definition: a word or phrase invented rather than inherited, often to name something new
senses.definitionCN: 非继承而来、通常为命名新事物而造出的词或短语
senses.example: The verb is a coinage of the nineteen-twenties, not an old farming word.
senses.exampleCN: 这个动词是二十世纪二十年代的新造词，并非古老的农事词。
senses.why: Striking a new piece of metal and striking a new word are the same gesture: something new is impressed with a known stamp.
senses.whyCN: 冲压一枚新币与造一个新词是同一动作：新东西被打上已知的印记。

senses.title: The act of inventing a word
senses.definition: the deliberate invention of vocabulary by a writer, a trade or an institution
senses.definitionCN: 由作者、行业或机构刻意创造词汇的行为
senses.example: His coinage of the term was mocked for a decade and then adopted everywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 他造的这个术语被嘲笑了十年，然后到处被采用。
senses.why: The countable act sense follows from the product sense, as with other -age nouns.
senses.whyCN: 可数的行为义由产物义引出，与其他 -age 名词一样。

senses.title: The right to strike coins
senses.definition: historical: the sovereign right to issue coin, often granted or leased to a mint
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法：发行硬币的君主权，常授予或租给造币厂
senses.example: The city held coinage rights for two centuries and grew rich on the fee.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市握有铸币权两个世纪，靠这项费用致富。
senses.why: A right over the tool becomes a right over the word, and coinage comes to mean the privilege itself.
senses.whyCN: 对工具的权利变成对词的权利，coinage 于是指这项特权本身。

senses.title: The quantity of coins issued
senses.definition: the amount of coin struck in a period, or one issue of a particular denomination
senses.definitionCN: 某时期铸造的硬币数量，或某一面额的某次发行
senses.example: The silver coinage of that year was recalled within a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年的银币在十年之内就被收回了。
senses.why: An uncountable product noun can be counted when a single issue or batch is meant.
senses.whyCN: 不可数的产物名词在指单次发行或单批时可以被计数。

senses.title: Something invented that passes as real
senses.definition: figuratively, a fabricated thing that circulates as if it were genuine, such as a coinage of propaganda
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指当作真物流传的编造之物，如宣传中造出的说法
senses.example: The phrase was a coinage of the ministry, repeated until it sounded like a fact.
senses.exampleCN: 这个说法是该部造出来的，被反复引用，直到听起来像事实。
senses.why: Counterfeit coin and counterfeit word share the idea of a stamp without the metal behind it.
senses.whyCN: 伪币与伪词共享同一观念：印记有了，背后却没有金属。

senses.title: A coined name for a product or place
senses.titleCN: 为产品或地方造出的名称
senses.definition: a commercial or official name invented for marketing rather than grown from the language
senses.definitionCN: 为营销或官方用途造出、而非从语言中自然长出的名称
senses.example: The brand is a coinage, built to be pronounceable in twelve languages.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌名是造出来的，为的是在十二种语言里都能念。
senses.why: Naming is the most commercial form of coining: a word is struck to circulate like a coin.
senses.whyCN: 命名是造词最商业化的形式：词被冲压出来，像硬币一样流通。

intro.en: Coinage begins with a wedge of metal, passes through a French word for the die, and ends up naming both money and new words.
intro.cn: coinage 从一块楔形金属开始，经过一个指模具的法语词，最后同时命名货币与新词。

items.en: Cuneus meant 'wedge'. The die that struck ancient coins was a wedge-shaped block, so the tool's name became the name of the thing struck.
items.cn: cuneus 意为「楔子」。冲压古币的模具是一块楔形物，于是工具之名成了被冲压之物的名字。

items.en: Old French coin meant 'die, stamp' and also 'corner, wedge'; English borrowed it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 coin 指「模具、印戳」，也指「角、楔」；英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: English first uses coin for the die and then for the piece of money, with the verb to coin following immediately.
items.cn: 英语先用 coin 指模具，随后指钱币，动词「铸造」随即跟上。

items.en: Moneta, the title of Juno whose temple housed the Roman mint, gives money and monetary by a separate route; it is not the source of coin.
items.cn: Moneta 是朱诺的称号，她的神庙设有罗马造币厂，经另一条路径给出 money 与 monetary；它不是 coin 的来源。

items.en: Coin plus the French suffix -age produces coinage, first for the act of minting and then for the coins themselves.
items.cn: coin 加法语后缀 -age 构成 coinage，先指铸造行为，再指硬币本身。

items.en: The word sense develops in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, when writers begin to speak of coining new terms as striking new pieces.
items.cn: 造词义在十六、十七世纪发展出来，当时写作者开始把造新术语说成冲压新币。

note.en: The first group is built on coin and its tool; the second holds words for money systems and for invented vocabulary.
note.cn: 第一组建于 coin 及其工具之上；第二组是货币体系与生造词汇的说法。

entries.definition: A single piece of money, or the act of striking one; coinage is the system, the process or the new word.
entries.definitionCN: 一枚钱币，或冲压它的动作；coinage 则是体系、过程或新词。

entries.definition: One who mints or one who invents words; the agent form of the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 铸币者或造词者；同一词干的施动形式。

entries.definition: Built like coinage but on mint: it means the quantity struck or the charge for striking.
entries.definitionCN: 与 coinage 同型但建于 mint：指铸造量或铸造费。

entries.definition: A compound for machines that take a coin; the word here is the object, not the system.
entries.definitionCN: 指投币机器的复合词；此处指物件，而非体系。

entries.definition: All money in use in a country, notes as well as coin; coinage covers only the metal part or the system behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 一国流通的全部货币，含纸币与硬币；coinage 只涵盖金属部分或其背后的体系。

entries.definition: The technical process of making coins; coinage also means the resulting system or the right to issue.
entries.definitionCN: 制币的技术过程；coinage 另指由此形成的体系或发行权。

entries.definition: The learned word for a new expression; coinage is the looser, more image-bearing term for the same thing.
entries.definitionCN: 指新表达的学术用词；coinage 是同一事物的更松散、更带比喻的说法。

entries.definition: Money a creditor must accept; it describes legal force, while coinage describes the stock of metal pieces.
entries.definitionCN: 债权人必须接受的货币；它描述法律效力，而 coinage 描述金属币的存量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: coin 'die' + -age 'process or product': the stamping and what it stamps out.
normal.cn: coin「模具」+ -age「过程或产物」：冲压的动作与被冲压出来的东西。

normal.en: The family runs coin, coinage, coiner, coining, coin-operated, and the parallel mintage.
normal.cn: 同族词有 coin、coinage、coiner、coining、coin-operated，以及同型的 mintage。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: decimal coinage, coinage rights, a new coinage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：十进制币制、铸币权、一个新造词。

normal.en: Money and words share the verb: you coin a phrase the way a mint coins a piece.
normal.cn: 钱与词共享同一个动词：你造一个短语，正如造币厂冲压一枚硬币。

normal.en: The word for the die survived inside the word for the money.
normal.cn: 指模具的词留在了指货币的词里面。

abstract.en: Picture a wedge-shaped die coming down on a blank and leaving a face where there was none.
abstract.cn: 想象一块楔形模具落在空白坯饼上，留下原本没有的一张脸。

abstract.en: Picture a phrase repeated by a ministry until listeners forget it was invented.
abstract.cn: 想象一个由某个部门反复使用的说法，直到听者忘了它是造出来的。

abstract.en: Picture a brand name tested in twelve languages before anyone hears it as a word.
abstract.cn: 想象一个品牌名在十二种语言里先试过，才被当作词听见。

examples.en: The colony had no coinage of its own and used whatever foreign silver arrived.
examples.cn: 这块殖民地没有自己的币制，有什么外国银币来就用什么。

examples.en: The word is a coinage of the nineteenth century, not a native term.
examples.cn: 这个词是十九世纪的新造词，不是本族语词。

examples.en: Coinage rights were leased to a family bank for a hundred years.
examples.cn: 铸币权被租给一家家族银行一百年。

dict_mnemonic.text: coin（模具、硬币）+ age（过程）＝ 打币这件事和打出来的币；再造个词，也是同一个动作。

root: 拉丁 cuneus「楔子」（模具为楔形）→ 古法语 coin「模具、印戳」→ 英语 coin「硬币；铸造」+ -age → coinage；与拉丁 moneta（造币厂）为不同来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from one struck blank to one invented word: the coin system, the minting, the new word, the act of inventing, the sovereign right, the quantity issued, the counterfeit, and the marketed name.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一枚被冲压的坯饼走到一个被造出的词：硬币体系、铸造、新词、造词行为、君主权、发行量、赝品，以及营销名称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wedge coming down on a blank disc, pressing a face into metal that had none.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块楔形模具落在空白圆片上，把一张脸压进原本没有脸的金属。

branches.en: STOCK AND ISSUE: the whole set of coins in use, then one batch struck in one year.
branches.cn: 存量与发行：流通中的整套硬币，再是某一年铸造的一批。

branches.en: WORK AND RIGHT: the labour of striking, and the sovereign permission that makes it legal.
branches.cn: 劳作与权利：冲压的劳动，以及使它合法的君主许可。

branches.en: STRUCK WORDS: a new term, and the act of inventing it.
branches.cn: 被冲压的词：新术语，以及造出它的行为。

branches.en: THE COUNTERFEIT: a stamp with nothing behind it, in metal or in language.
branches.cn: 赝品：有印记而背后无物，金属如此，语言亦如此。

branches.en: THE NAME THAT TRAVELS: a coined label built so that strangers will repeat it in a market.
branches.cn: 会走动的名字：为让陌生人在市场上反复念出来而造的品牌名。

intro.en: Coinage is a Latin-derived noun for a die plus a French suffix for process and product, and the family it belongs to still speaks of both metal and words.
intro.cn: coinage 是一个源自拉丁、指模具的名词加一个法语后缀构成，后者表过程与产物；它所属的词族至今同时谈论金属与词语。

latinIntro.en: Latin cuneus 'wedge' gives coin and coinage through French coin; Latin moneta, the mint, gives money and monetary by a separate line. The two are often confused because both concern coins.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cuneus「楔子」经法语 coin 给出 coin 与 coinage；拉丁 moneta（造币厂）经另一条线给出 money 与 monetary。两者常被混淆，因为都与硬币有关。

items.example: The die was a wedge, and the tool named the coin.
items.exampleCN: 模具是楔形的，工具便给硬币命了名。

items.meaning: a die; a piece of money
items.example: The noun still names both ends of the process.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词仍兼指过程的两端。

items.example: The suffix builds many nouns of activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成许多表活动的名词。

items.example: The compound noun is the abstract form.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合名词是抽象形式。

items.example: The agent form serves both domains.
items.exampleCN: 这个施动形式在两个领域都可用。

items.example: The gerund keeps the process in view.
items.exampleCN: 这个动名词把过程留在视野中。

items.example: The compound refers to the object, not the system.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指物件，而非体系。

items.example: The parallel noun shows the same suffix at work.
items.exampleCN: 这个同型名词显示同一后缀的运作。

items.example: A different root gives money and monetary.
items.exampleCN: 另一词根给出 money 与 monetary。

definition_zh: 同时发生；位置重合；完全一致；巧合
definition_en: to fall on the same point in time or space, or to agree exactly
core_image: 两条本来分开的轨迹，最后落到同一个点上
scene: 这组词中，Two friends meet on the platform and one says: What a coincidence — our trains coincided by the minute.
sceneCN: 这里 coincide 是「（时间上）同时发生、恰好重合」（第 1 个义项）；句意：真巧，我们两趟车分秒不差地同时到站。画面里是站台、两只对上的手表和同一块站牌。

senses.title: Time: two events land on one moment
senses.titleCN: 同时发生：两件事落在同一个时刻
senses.definition: to happen at the same time as something else
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事同时发生
senses.example: The conference coincides with the start of the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 会议恰好与收割的开始同时。
senses.why: The Latin verb was com- 'together' + incidere 'to fall upon'. Two events coincide when they fall on the same instant, as two arrows hitting one mark.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词是 com-“一起”+ incidere“落到……上”。两件事同时发生，就是它们落到同一个瞬间，像两支箭射中同一个点。

senses.title: Space: two things occupy one place
senses.titleCN: 位置重合：两物占着同一处空间
senses.definition: to occupy the same space or position
senses.definitionCN: 占据同一空间或位置
senses.example: The two beams coincide at the centre of the lens.
senses.exampleCN: 两束光在透镜中心重合。
senses.why: Falling together in space is the literal image: two bodies descend onto one point and can no longer be told apart by position.
senses.whyCN: 在空间里“一起落下”是最字面的意象：两个物体落到同一个点上，位置再也分不出彼此。

senses.title: Identity: two things turn out to be one
senses.titleCN: 同一：两样东西其实是同一个
senses.definition: to be identical in substance or nature with something else
senses.definitionCN: 在实质或性质上与另一事物完全相同
senses.example: His account of the night coincides exactly with hers.
senses.exampleCN: 他对那晚的叙述与她的完全一致。
senses.why: If two descriptions fall on the same point, the gap between them disappears. Coinciding here means the two versions cannot be separated by any detail.
senses.whyCN: 如果两份叙述落到同一点上，它们之间的缝隙就消失了。这里的重合指两个版本在任何细节上都分不开。

senses.title: Opinion: two minds meet on a point
senses.titleCN: 意见一致：两个头脑在一点上相遇
senses.definition: of views or interests, to agree or be in harmony
senses.definitionCN: （观点或利益）一致或和谐
senses.example: Our views on the merger coincide almost completely.
senses.exampleCN: 我们对合并的看法几乎完全一致。
senses.why: Opinions are paths that can arrive at the same conclusion. When they coincide, two people stand on one point, even if they started from different places.
senses.whyCN: 意见是可能抵达同一结论的路径。当它们重合，两个人就站在同一个点上，哪怕出发处不同。

senses.title: Geometry: lines laid on lines
senses.titleCN: 几何重合：线与线叠在一起
senses.definition: of geometric points, lines or figures, to occupy exactly the same position
senses.definitionCN: （几何的点、线或图形）占据完全相同的位置
senses.example: If the two circles coincide, every point on one lies on the other.
senses.exampleCN: 如果两个圆重合，一个圆上的每一点都在另一个圆上。
senses.why: Geometry strips away everything but position. Coinciding figures are two names for one set of points, the purest case of 'falling on the same spot'.
senses.whyCN: 几何剥掉了一切，只剩位置。重合的图形是同一组点的两个名字，这是“落到同一处”最纯粹的情形。

senses.title: Calendar: a date falls on another date
senses.titleCN: 日期相撞：一个日子落在另一个日子上
senses.definition: of dates or occasions, to fall on the same day
senses.definitionCN: （日期或场合）落在同一天
senses.example: Her birthday coincides with the first day of the spring festival.
senses.exampleCN: 她的生日恰好是春节的第一天。
senses.why: Calendars are grids of slots; two occasions coincide when they drop into one slot. The metaphor is spatial, but the space is made of dates.
senses.whyCN: 日历是一格一格的槽；两个日子同时落进同一格，就是重合。比喻是空间的，只是这个空间由日期构成。

senses.title: Chance: a meeting that was not arranged
senses.titleCN: 巧合：并非安排却撞在一起
senses.definition: of events, to happen together by chance, without a planned connection
senses.definitionCN: （事件）偶然同时发生，并无计划中的联系
senses.example: Their arrivals coincided, though neither knew the other was coming.
senses.exampleCN: 他们同时到达，尽管谁也不知道对方会来。
senses.why: The word describes the landing, not the cause. When two paths meet without a planner, the meeting looks like chance, and coincidence becomes the name for that surprise.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述的是“落点”，不是原因。两条路径在没有安排者的情况下相遇，这次相遇就显得偶然，coincidence 便成了这种意外的名字。

senses.title: Fit: a result lands on what was wanted
senses.titleCN: 相符：结果正好落在所愿之处
senses.definition: to correspond exactly to a need, wish or expectation
senses.definitionCN: 与需求、愿望或预期完全相符
senses.example: The new branch's opening coincided with a surge in demand.
senses.exampleCN: 新分店的开业恰逢需求激增。
senses.why: When an outcome falls on the exact point a plan aimed at, we say the two coincide. Here chance and fit merge: the event lands where it was needed.
senses.whyCN: 当结果正好落在计划瞄准的那一点，我们说二者重合。此处偶然与契合合并：事件落在正需要它的地方。

senses.title: Astrology: planets falling into one house
senses.titleCN: 星象同宫：行星落进同一个位置
senses.definition: in medieval astrology, of two planets, to occupy the same degree of the zodiac
senses.definitionCN: 在中世纪占星术中，（两颗行星）占据黄道同一度数
senses.example: Medieval tables noted when Saturn and Jupiter coincided.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的星表会记下土星与木星何时同宫。
senses.why: Medieval Latin coincidere was an astrological term for planets 'falling upon together' in one degree. The modern word kept the geometry and dropped the stars.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 coincidere 是占星术语，指行星“一起落到”同一度数。现代词保留了这层几何，丢掉了星辰。

intro.en: Coincide is built from 'together' and 'to fall'. Its whole history is one picture: two things falling onto the same point, whether that point is a moment, a place, a date or a conclusion.
intro.cn: coincide 由“一起”和“落下”构成。它的整部历史就是一个画面：两样东西落到同一个点上，无论这个点是时刻、地点、日期还是结论。

items.en: Coincidere meant literally 'to fall upon together'. It was used in astrology for planets occupying the same degree of the zodiac.
items.cn: coincidere 字面意为“一起落到……上”。它在中世纪占星术中指行星占据黄道同一度数。

items.en: The Latin verb coincidere was used in English writing from the 1640s, still close to its 'fall together' image.
items.cn: 拉丁动词 coincidere 从 1640 年代起在英语写作中使用，仍贴近“一起落下”的意象。

items.en: The English verb is recorded in 1705 as 'be identical in substance or nature', the sense in which two accounts or natures cannot be told apart.
items.cn: 英语动词记录于 1705 年，意为“在实质或性质上完全相同”，即两份叙述或两种性质无法分辨。

items.en: By 1715 it meant 'occupy the same space, agree in position', restoring the literal geometry of two bodies at one point.
items.cn: 到 1715 年，它表示“占据同一空间、位置相符”，恢复了两物在同一地点的字面几何。

items.en: The everyday modern sense 'occur at the same time' is recorded from 1809, extending the same point from space to the clock.
items.cn: 日常现代义“同时发生”记录于 1809 年，把同一个“点”从空间延伸到时钟。

items.en: Cadere 'to fall' is traced to PIE *kad- 'to fall', also behind accident, incident, occasion and cadence. The reconstructed root has no written record, so the deepest step is source uncertain.
items.cn: cadere“落下”被追溯到原始印欧语 *kad-“落下”，accident、incident、occasion、cadence 也出自这里。该重构词根没有书面记录，故最深层来源不确定。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: a surprising happening of two events at once, or the state of occupying the same position. It is the noun of coincide.
entries.definitionCN: 巧合；同时发生；重合。它是 coincide 的名词。

entries.definition: an event, often an unpleasant one. It comes from the same cadere 'to fall', literally 'a thing that falls upon one'.
entries.definitionCN: 事件，常指不愉快的事。它同出 cadere“落下”，字面是“落到某人身上的事”。

entries.definition: the rate at which something occurs. It shares the -cid- root but means frequency, not overlap.
entries.definitionCN: 发生率。它同样有 -cid- 词根，但指频率，不是重合。

entries.definition: to settle a question or choice. It looks close but comes from de- + caedere 'to cut', not cadere 'to fall'.
entries.definitionCN: 决定。它形近，但来自 de- + caedere“切”，不是 cadere“落”。

entries.definition: to agree in opinion, or to happen at the same time. It matches both the opinion and time senses.
entries.definitionCN: 同意；同时发生。它同时对应观点义与时间义。

entries.definition: to match or be equivalent to something. It stresses a correspondence between two sets, not a landing on one point.
entries.definitionCN: 相符；对应。它强调两个集合之间的对应，而非落到同一点。

entries.definition: to cover part of the same area or time. It is a partial coincidence, not a complete one.
entries.definitionCN: 部分重叠。它是部分重合，而非完全重合。

entries.definition: to be equal or similar to something. It is the everyday word for the 'agree exactly' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 相配；相符。它是“完全一致”一义最日常的说法。

entries.definition: to make two things happen at the same time. It is intentional, whereas coincide is usually not.
entries.definitionCN: 使同步。它是刻意安排的，而 coincide 通常不是。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin com- and cadere, the -cid- family, and the derived forms English actually uses.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 com- 与 cadere、-cid- 词族，以及英语实际使用的派生形式。

normal.en: coincide = co- 'together' + in- 'upon' + cadere 'to fall': two things fall onto one spot.
normal.cn: coincide = co-“一起”+ in-“落在……上”+ cadere“落”：两样东西落到同一个点上。

normal.en: The same cadere gives accident, incident, occasion and cadence, all built on something falling or happening.
normal.cn: 同一个 cadere 还给出 accident、incident、occasion、cadence，都建立在“落下、发生”上。

normal.en: In astrology, coincidere meant two planets falling into the same degree; the modern word keeps the geometry and drops the stars.
normal.cn: 在占星术里，coincidere 指两颗行星落到同一度数；现代词保留了这层几何，丢掉了星辰。

normal.en: A coincidence is simply two paths landing on one point when nobody planned it.
normal.cn: 巧合就是没人安排时，两条路径落到同一个点上。

normal.en: When two watches agree to the second, their readings coincide; when two people agree on a plan, their minds do.
normal.cn: 两只手表对到同一秒，读数重合；两个人同意一个计划，头脑也重合。

abstract.en: The core operation is two independent paths arriving at one point, whether in space, time or thought.
abstract.cn: 核心动作是两条独立的路径抵达同一个点，无论在空间、时间还是思想上。

abstract.en: What changes is only the kind of point: a degree of the zodiac, a coordinate, a date, a minute, a conclusion.
abstract.cn: 变化的只是“点”的种类：黄道度数、坐标、日期、分钟、结论。

abstract.en: So 'happen together', 'overlap', 'be identical' and 'agree' are one event seen at different scales of precision.
abstract.cn: 所以“同时发生、重合、完全相同、意见一致”是同一个事件在不同精度上被看到。

examples.en: The festival coincides with the end of the school term.
examples.cn: 这个节日恰逢学期结束。

examples.en: Her interests coincide with those of the research group.
examples.cn: 她的兴趣与研究小组的一致。

examples.en: The two triangles coincide exactly when folded.
examples.cn: 折叠时这两个三角形完全重合。

dict_mnemonic.text: co（一起）+ in（进来）+ cide（像 side 边）——两条边一起进到同一处 → coincide 重合、同时发生

root: 源自中世纪拉丁语 coincidere“一起落到……上”，由 com-“一起”+ incidere“落到”（in- 上 + cadere 落）构成，核心是“落到同一个点”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of coincide, all traced to one act: falling onto the same point. The point may be a moment, a place, a date, a degree of the sky or a conclusion; in every case two paths meet at one mark.
sensesIntro.cn: coincide 的九个义项都追溯到一个动作：落到同一个点上。这个点可以是时刻、地点、日期、天上的度数或结论；每一次都是两条路径在同一点相遇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two separate paths landing on one exact point.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条分开的路径落在同一个精确的点上。

branches.en: TIME MEETS: events fall on one moment, and dates fall into one slot of the calendar.
branches.cn: 时间相遇：事件落到同一个时刻，日期落进日历的同一格。

branches.en: SPACE MEETS: bodies share one location, and geometric figures lie exactly on one another.
branches.cn: 空间相遇：物体共享同一位置，几何图形正好叠在彼此上面。

branches.en: MINDS MEET: two accounts cannot be told apart, and two opinions stand on one point.
branches.cn: 头脑相遇：两份叙述无法分辨，两个意见站在同一个点上。

branches.en: CHANCE AND FIT: paths cross without a planner, or land exactly where a plan needed them.
branches.cn: 偶然与契合：路径在没有安排者时交叉，或正好落在计划需要的地方。

branches.en: THE OLD SKY: astrology had two planets falling into one degree, the original technical use.
branches.cn: 古老的天空：占星术中两颗行星落入同一度数，这是最早的技术用法。

intro.en: Coincide is co- + in- + cadere. Its family shows the prefixes com-/co- and in-, the fall-root cad-, and the noun suffixes -ence and -al.
intro.cn: coincide 是 co- + in- + cadere。它的词族展示了前缀 com-/co- 与 in-、表“落”的词根 cad-，以及名词后缀 -ence、-al。

latinIntro.en: Latin cadere 'to fall' is the root of a large family: incident, accident, occasion, cadence and coincidence. Medieval Latin coincidere joined com- with incidere, literally 'to fall upon together'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cadere“落下”是一个大词族的根：incident、accident、occasion、cadence、coincidence。中世纪拉丁语 coincidere 把 com- 与 incidere 结合，字面即“一起落到……上”。

items.meaning: to fall on the same point; to agree exactly
items.meaningCN: 同时发生；重合；一致（co- 一起，in- 在上，cadere 落）
items.example: My holiday coincides with hers.
items.exampleCN: 我的假期和她的重合。

items.meaning: a chance happening of two events at once; the state of overlapping
items.meaningCN: 巧合；同时发生；重合（-ence 构成名词）
items.example: By coincidence, we sat next to each other.
items.exampleCN: 碰巧，我们坐在了一起。

items.meaning: happening at the same time or occupying the same position
items.meaningCN: 同时发生的；重合的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.example: The two events were coincident by chance.
items.exampleCN: 这两个事件偶然同时发生。

items.meaning: resulting from chance rather than planning
items.meaningCN: 巧合的；偶然的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The similarity is purely coincidental.
items.exampleCN: 这种相似纯属巧合。

items.meaning: by chance; at the same time
items.meaningCN: 碰巧；巧合地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Coincidentally, they had both applied for the same job.
items.exampleCN: 碰巧，他们俩都申请了同一份工作。

items.meaning: the rate at which something happens
items.meaningCN: 发生率；发病率（同根 cadere，-ence 构成名词）
items.example: The incidence of the disease has fallen.
items.exampleCN: 这种病的发病率已经下降。

items.meaning: an event that falls upon someone; a minor disturbance
items.meaningCN: 事件；小事故（同根 cadere，-ent 构成名词）
items.example: The incident was reported to the police.

definition_zh: 合作；协作；（与占领者）通敌；协助
definition_en: to work together with others on a task, or, in a hostile sense, to help an enemy or an occupier
core_image: 两双手在同一架织机上同时操作，各自负责一半
scene: 实验室里，两组人把各自测到的数据摊在同一张大桌上对照。The two universities agreed to collaborate on a study of coastal erosion.
sceneCN: 这里 collaborate 指「两个团队共同完成一项工作」（第 1 个义项：合作共事）；句意为两所大学同意就海岸侵蚀问题合作开展研究。可辨识物件：大桌、两摞数据表、坐标纸、显微镜。

senses.title: Work jointly on a task
senses.definition: to work with one or more others toward a shared result
senses.definitionCN: 与一个或几个人一起朝共同的结果努力
senses.example: The two universities agreed to collaborate on a study of coastal erosion.
senses.exampleCN: 两所大学同意就海岸侵蚀问题合作开展研究。
senses.why: the Latin verb joins com- 'together' to laborare 'to work', so the core reading is simply working together.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词把 com-「共同」与 laborare「劳动」接在一起，核心意思就是「一起干活」。

senses.title: Create a work together
senses.definition: of writers, artists or musicians, to produce a work jointly
senses.definitionCN: 指作家、艺术家或音乐家共同产生一件作品
senses.example: The novelist collaborated with a photographer on the book.
senses.exampleCN: 小说家与一位摄影师合作完成了这本书。
senses.why: joint work in the arts is the same act as joint work in a lab, only the product is a work rather than a result.
senses.whyCN: 艺术上的共同劳作与实验室里的共同劳作是同一个动作，只是产物是作品而非结果。

senses.title: Institutions pooling resources
senses.definition: of organizations, to run a programme or a study together
senses.definitionCN: 指机构共同运行一个项目或一项研究
senses.example: Three hospitals collaborated on the vaccine trial.
senses.exampleCN: 三家医院合作开展了疫苗试验。
senses.why: large bodies cannot work side by side, so the verb comes to mean pooling staff, data and money.
senses.whyCN: 大型机构无法并肩干活，于是这个动词转为「共享人力、数据与经费」。

senses.title: Help an occupying enemy
senses.definition: to cooperate with an enemy that has taken control of one's country
senses.definitionCN: 与已经控制本国的敌人合作
senses.example: Those who collaborated with the occupiers faced trial after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 那些与占领者合作的人在战后受到审判。
senses.why: the word for working together darkened in wartime, because working with an occupier is a kind of cooperation too.
senses.whyCN: 「一起干活」这个词在战时变了颜色，因为与占领者一起干活，也是一种合作。

senses.title: Knowingly assist wrongdoing
senses.definition: to give help to a person or a scheme one knows to be harmful
senses.definitionCN: 对明知有害的人或计划提供帮助
senses.example: The clerk was accused of collaborating in the fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 那名职员被指控在诈骗中予以协助。
senses.why: help is help whatever the cause, so the negative sense spreads from politics to crime and misconduct.
senses.whyCN: 帮助就是帮助，不论缘由，于是这个负面义从政治扩散到犯罪与不当行为。

senses.title: Cooperate with a request
senses.definition: to go along with someone's plan or request in an ordinary, neutral way
senses.definitionCN: 以平常、中性的方式配合某人的计划或请求
senses.example: The witnesses collaborated fully with the inquiry.
senses.exampleCN: 证人们全力配合了调查。
senses.why: this is the neutral middle of the word: not a shared project, but not betrayal either.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的中性地带：既不是共同项目，也不是背叛。

senses.title: Work with a rival
senses.definition: to work alongside a competitor on a matter of common interest
senses.definitionCN: 在与竞争对手有共同利益的事项上一起工作
senses.example: Rival airlines collaborated on the safety guidelines.
senses.exampleCN: 相互竞争的航空公司合作制定了安全准则。
senses.why: the word can hold opposites at once: parties stay rivals and still share the work.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以同时容纳相反的两面：各方仍是竞争对手，却仍分担同一份工作。

senses.title: Systems working in tandem
senses.definition: of software, equipment or teams, to operate together smoothly
senses.definitionCN: 指软件、设备或团队顺畅地一起运作
senses.example: The two programs collaborate through a shared protocol.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个程序通过一套共享协议协同工作。
senses.why: machines are given the human verb when their parts must act as one, the newest branch of the word.
senses.whyCN: 当机器的各部分必须像一体那样行动，就给它用了这个属人的动词，这是最新的一支。

intro.en: Collaborate comes from Latin collaborare, com- 'together' plus laborare 'to work'. English borrowed it in the nineteenth century; the traitorous sense arrived in the 1940s. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: collaborate 来自拉丁 collaborare，由 com-「共同」与 laborare「劳动」构成。英语在十九世纪借入；「通敌」义在二十世纪四十年代出现。年代均为约数。

items.en: Labor meant 'toil, effort, hardship'. Its deeper origin is not established, and forms proposed for it before Latin exist only as reconstructions.
items.cn: labor 意为「辛劳、费力、艰苦」。其更深来源没有定论，为它在拉丁语之前提出的形式只以重构形式存在。

items.en: The verb laborare meant 'to work, toil, suffer hardship', and it also underlies English elaborate and laboratory through related forms.
items.cn: 动词 laborare 意为「劳作、辛苦、受苦」，它还经相关形式构成英语的 elaborate 与 laboratory。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus laborare produced collaborare, 'to work together', a plain compound with no special legal or political colour.
items.cn: com-「共同」加 laborare 得出 collaborare「一起劳作」，是一个平实的复合词，不带法律或政治色彩。

items.en: English took the verb in the nineteenth century, first in writing about science, literature and public works.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪借入这个动词，最初见于关于科学、文学与公共工程的写作。

items.en: In the 1940s the noun was applied to those who cooperated with an occupying power, and the verb took on that stigma.
items.cn: 二十世纪四十年代，这个名词被用于指与占领当局合作的人，动词也随之带上这层污名。

items.en: Source uncertain (first citation): the earliest English use is dated differently across dictionaries, and the pre-Latin history of labor is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见书证）：各家词典对最早的英语用例说法不一；labor 在拉丁语之前的历史属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same working root or on similar shapes; group two holds verbs of joint action, from neutral to suspicious.
note.cn: 第一组收同出「劳作」词根或形近的词；第二组收表示共同行动的动词，从中性到可疑。

entries.definition: From e- 'out' plus laborare: to work something out in detail, so it shares the working root but not the togetherness.
entries.definitionCN: 由 e-「向外」加 laborare 构成：把某事做细做透，与「劳作」同根，却没有「共同」之意。

entries.definition: From Latin laborare through a place noun: a room for work, not a act of working with others.
entries.definitionCN: 经一个地点名词出自拉丁 laborare：干活的房间，而不是与他人共同劳作的行为。

entries.definition: From Latin roborare 'to strengthen', built on robur 'oak, strength': to confirm, with no link to working.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 roborare「使强固」，由 robur「橡木、力量」构成：意为证实，与「劳作」无关。

entries.definition: The noun of this verb: joint work, or, in the wartime sense, cooperation with an enemy.
entries.definitionCN: 本动词的名词：共同的工作，或战时意义上的通敌合作。

entries.definition: To do what is asked or needed for a shared aim; it stresses willingness rather than shared creation.
entries.definitionCN: 为共同目标做被请求或需要的事；侧重「愿意配合」，而非共同创造。

entries.definition: An everyday phrase for joining forces, usually for a specific occasion.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指合在一起干，通常为某件具体的事。

entries.definition: A phrase for combining strength, often against a common opponent or problem.
entries.definitionCN: 指把力量合起来，常针对共同的对手或难题。

entries.definition: To work together in secret for a dishonest purpose; the negative intent is built into the word.
entries.definitionCN: 为不正当目的暗中串通；负面意图已含在词里。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Com- 'together' plus laborare 'work': two people at one bench.
normal.cn: com-「共同」加 laborare「劳动」：两个人共用一张工作台。

normal.en: The family runs collaborate, collaboration, collaborator, collaborative, collaborationist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 collaborate、collaboration、collaborator、collaborative、collaborationist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases ask who and what: collaborate with a team, collaborate on a study.
normal.cn: 固定搭配问「和谁、做什么」：与团队合作、就一项研究合作。

normal.en: The wartime sense is always marked: collaborate with the enemy.
normal.cn: 战时的义项总带标记：与敌人合作。

normal.en: The relative elaborate drops the togetherness and keeps only the working out.
normal.cn: 近形的 elaborate 去掉了「共同」，只留下「做细做透」。

intro.en: Collaborate is a Latin compound verb whose prefix and root still build English words, so the whole family reads morpheme by morpheme.

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 laborare 衍生 labor、elaborate 与 laboratory，而 com- 增添「与他人一起」之意。

definition_en: the act of working jointly with others on a shared task or project

scene: 两个实验室把各自的样本和数据放在同一张桌上，轮流守夜跑完整个实验。The collaboration between the two labs produced a result neither could have reached alone.
sceneCN: 这里 collaboration 指两个以上主体共同投入、完成一项工作的合作（第 1 个义项：共同劳动）；句意为两个实验室的合作产生了任何一方单独都无法达到的结果。

一项具体的合作项目（可数，用复数 collaborations）

derivatives.zh: 合作；协作（由拉丁 collaborare「一起劳动」经法语进入英语，保留「共同出力」的动作义）
协作的；合作的（由 collaborate 加表示「倾向」的后缀构成，转指以共同参与为特征）
合作者；协作者（由 collaborate 加表示「人」的后缀构成，转指共同出力的人）
实验室（同出拉丁 laborare「劳动」，由「劳作之处」转指进行实验的场所）
详述；精心制作的（由表示「向外」的拉丁前缀加 laborare 构成，从「费力做出」转指细致加工）
费力的；艰苦的（由拉丁 labor「劳动」加表示「充满」的后缀构成，转指劳动量很大）

senses.title: Working together on a shared task
senses.definition: the act of two or more people or groups working jointly on the same task
senses.definitionCN: 两个以上的人或团体共同投入同一项工作的行为
senses.example: The collaboration between the two labs produced a result neither could have reached alone.
senses.exampleCN: 两个实验室的合作产生了任何一方单独都无法达到的结果。
senses.why: Collaboration is labour shared: the Latin verb joins 'together' to 'work', so the core is joint effort rather than mere contact.
senses.whyCN: collaboration 是共享的劳动：拉丁动词把「一起」接到「劳动」上，核心是共同出力，而非仅仅接触。

senses.title: Joint authorship or creation
senses.definition: the state of producing a book, work of art or invention together, with shared credit
senses.definitionCN: 共同完成书籍、艺术品或发明，并共享署名
senses.example: The album is a collaboration between a composer and a field recordist.
senses.exampleCN: 这张专辑是一位作曲家与一位野外录音师的共同创作。
senses.why: When the joint work leaves a named product, the word shifts from the activity to the shared credit.
senses.whyCN: 当共同劳动留下具名成品，词义就从活动转到共享的署名。

senses.title: Wartime cooperation with an occupier
senses.definition: the act of working with an enemy occupier, treated as betrayal by compatriots
senses.definitionCN: 与敌方占领者合作，被同胞视为背叛的行为
senses.example: The post-war trials punished wartime collaboration with the occupying army.
senses.exampleCN: 战后审判惩罚了战时与占领军合作的行为。
senses.why: History gave the neutral word a dark sense: working together becomes treason when the partner is an enemy.
senses.whyCN: 历史给这个中性词添了黑暗义：当伙伴是敌人时，共同工作就变成叛国。

senses.title: Cross-disciplinary collaboration
senses.definition: joint work between specialists from different fields, each contributing a distinct method
senses.definitionCN: 不同领域的专家共同工作，各自贡献不同方法
senses.example: The climate report required collaboration between physicists and historians.
senses.exampleCN: 这份气候报告需要物理学家与历史学家协作。
senses.why: Complex problems no longer fit one department, so the word names the bridge between different expert languages.
senses.whyCN: 复杂问题不再属于单一部门，因此这个词命名不同专家语言之间的桥。

senses.title: Digital collaboration tools
senses.definition: the use of shared software and networks so that people can work on one file or project at a distance
senses.definitionCN: 使用共享软件与网络，使人们能远程处理同一文件或项目
senses.example: Remote collaboration improved once the team shared one editing space.
senses.exampleCN: 团队共用同一个编辑空间后，远程协作改善了。
senses.why: Technology extends the same joint labour across distance, turning a room into a network.
senses.whyCN: 技术把同一种共同劳动拉过距离，把一间屋子变成一张网络。

senses.title: A business partnership
senses.definition: a working arrangement between firms or departments for a shared commercial goal
senses.definitionCN: 企业或部门为共同商业目标形成的合作安排
senses.example: The two firms announced a collaboration to build the charging network.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司宣布合作建设充电网络。
senses.why: Commerce uses the word for a bounded arrangement: the parties remain separate but pool part of their work.
senses.whyCN: 商业用这个词指有边界的安排：各方仍独立，但把部分工作合在一起。

senses.title: Scientific collaboration
senses.definition: joint research by scientists who share data, instruments or authorship across institutions
senses.definitionCN: 科学家跨机构共享数据、仪器或署名权的研究合作
senses.example: The discovery rested on a long collaboration across three continents.
senses.exampleCN: 这项发现依赖横跨三大洲的长期合作。
senses.why: Big science is rarely solitary, so the word becomes the normal label for shared instruments and shared papers.
senses.whyCN: 大科学很少单干，因此这个词成为共享仪器与共享论文的常规标签。

senses.title: Abstract: effort greater than its parts
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：合力超过部分之和
senses.definition: joint effort whose result exceeds what the participants could produce separately
senses.definitionCN: 其结果超过参与者各自单独所能产出的共同出力
senses.example: The essay argues that collaboration is not addition but a third mind.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章主张合作不是相加，而是生出第三个头脑。
senses.why: At its most abstract the word names the surplus that appears when separate skills interlock.
senses.whyCN: 推到最抽象处，这个词命名不同技能咬合时出现的盈余。

intro.en: Collaboration comes from Latin collaborare 'to work together', from com- 'together' plus laborare 'to work'. It entered English in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: collaboration 来自拉丁 collaborare「一起劳动」，由表示「一起」的成分加 laborare「劳动」构成。它在十九世纪进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Labor meant 'work, toil, effort', and also 'a task'. It is the noun behind laborious and laboratory.
items.cn: labor 意为「劳动、辛苦、努力」，也指「一项任务」。它是 laborious 与 laboratory 背后的名词。

items.en: Laborare meant 'to work, toil, take pains'. The verb keeps the physical effort of the noun.
items.cn: laborare 意为「劳动、辛苦、费心」。这个动词保留了名词里的体力付出。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus laborare produced collaborare 'to work together'. The Latin verb had no political colour.
items.cn: 表示「一起」的成分加 laborare 构成 collaborare「一起劳动」。这个拉丁动词没有政治色彩。

items.en: French collaboration and English collaboration appeared in the nineteenth century for joint work in science, letters and business.
items.cn: 法语 collaboration 与英语 collaboration 在十九世纪出现，指科学、文学与商业中的共同工作。

items.en: During the Second World War the same word was applied to cooperation with an occupying power, and this negative sense became fixed in many languages.
items.cn: 第二次世界大战期间，同一个词被用于指与占领国合作，这一负面义在多种语言中固定下来。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the first printed English use of collaboration is not precisely recorded, and the exact date when the wartime sense became standard is disputed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：collaboration 在英语中最早印行于何时没有精确记录；战时义何时成为标准说法也有争议。

note.en: Group one separates the word from other Latin verbs of working together; group two holds the everyday names for joint work.
note.cn: 第一组把这个词与其他表示共同工作的拉丁动词分开；第二组是共同劳动的日常说法。

entries.definition: From Latin cooperari, built on operari 'to work' and opus 'work'. It stresses mutual help more than a shared project.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 cooperari，基底是 operari「工作」与 opus「工作」。它更强调互相帮助，而非共同项目。

entries.definition: From Latin ordinare 'to arrange in order'. It means keeping activities in step, not doing the work together.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 ordinare「按次序安排」。它指让活动步调一致，而非一起做同一件事。

entries.definition: From Latin colludere 'to play together', built on ludere 'to play'. It means a secret, often dishonest agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 colludere「一起玩」，基底是 ludere「玩」。它指秘密且常不正当的串通。

entries.definition: From Latin collega, built on legare 'to send as a deputy', not laborare. A colleague is a fellow worker, not the joint work.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 collega，基底是 legare「派为使节」，并非 laborare。同事是一起工作的人，不是共同工作本身。

entries.definition: The everyday noun for people working well together; collaboration is its formal and project-oriented counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指人们配合良好的日常名词；collaboration 是其正式、以项目为导向的对应词。

entries.definition: A formal arrangement between parties, often legal and long-term; collaboration can be a single project.
entries.definitionCN: 各方之间的正式安排，常带法律与长期性质；collaboration 可以只是一个项目。

entries.definition: Willing help offered to another's effort; it does not require a shared product or shared credit.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意协助他人的努力；它不要求共同成品或共同署名。

entries.definition: A formal union of parties for a common aim, usually political or military; it stresses the bond rather than the work.
entries.definitionCN: 各方为共同目标结成的正式联盟，通常指政治或军事；它强调纽带而非劳动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定说法与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Laborare means to work, so collaboration is literally working together.
normal.cn: laborare 意为劳动，所以 collaboration 字面上就是一起劳动。

normal.en: The 'together' prefix is the same one in collect and cooperate, but only this verb attaches it to work.
normal.cn: 表示「一起」的前缀与 collect、cooperate 相同，但只有这个动词把它接到「劳动」上。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scale: research collaboration, international collaboration, in collaboration with.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出尺度：研究合作、国际合作、与……合作。

normal.en: Laboratory shares the work root: a place of work became a place of experiment.
normal.cn: laboratory 共享「劳动」词根：劳作之处变成了实验之处。

normal.en: The wartime sense is the dark twin: the same joint work, now with an enemy.
normal.cn: 战时义是它的黑暗双生：同一种共同劳动，伙伴换成了敌人。

abstract.en: Picture two people holding opposite ends of one rope around a heavy stone.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人各执一根绳子的两端，绕着一块沉重的石头。

abstract.en: Picture two hands correcting the same drawing, each line continuing the other.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在同一张图上改线，每条线都接着另一条。

abstract.en: Picture a third mind appearing between two speakers as they talk.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人说话时，在他们之间出现第三个头脑。

examples.en: The bridge was built through collaboration between engineers and local masons.
examples.cn: 这座桥由工程师与本地石匠合作建成。

examples.en: International collaboration shortened the vaccine trial by years.
examples.cn: 国际合作把疫苗试验缩短了数年。

examples.en: The wartime collaboration still divides the town's memory.
examples.cn: 战时的通敌合作至今仍分裂着这座镇的记忆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可 拉伯 雷 申」——一起出力把重东西抬起来 → 合作

root: 拉丁 collaborare「一起劳动」= 表示「一起」的成分 + laborare「劳动」；后者来自 labor「劳动」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start with shared labour, then move to shared credit, wartime betrayal, cross-disciplinary work, remote tools, business deals, big science and finally the surplus that appears when skills interlock.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从共同劳动出发，转到共享署名、战时背叛、跨学科工作、远程工具、商业协议、大科学，最后是技能咬合时出现的盈余。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands on one rope, a heavy stone between them, neither able to lift it alone.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手握同一根绳，中间是一块沉重的石头，谁都单独抬不起来。

branches.en: WORK AND CREDIT: joint labour, then the shared name on what it produces.
branches.cn: 劳动与署名：先是共同出力，再是成品上的共同名字。

branches.en: THE DARK TWIN: the same joint work performed with an enemy occupier.
branches.cn: 黑暗双生：同一种共同劳动，伙伴换成敌方占领者。

branches.en: ACROSS BORDERS: different disciplines and different institutions pool methods and instruments.
branches.cn: 跨越边界：不同学科与不同机构共享方法与仪器。

branches.en: TOOLS AND CONTRACTS: software carries the work across distance, and firms bound it with an agreement.
branches.cn: 工具与合同：软件把劳动拉过距离，公司用协议给它划界。

branches.en: SURPLUS: the result exceeds what any participant could make alone.
branches.cn: 盈余：结果超过任何参与者单独所能做出。

intro.en: Collaboration is a Latin verb of work with a prefix meaning 'together', plus a noun ending.
intro.cn: collaboration 是一个表示劳动的拉丁动词，带表示「一起」的前缀，再加名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin labor gives laborious and laboratory; laborare gives collaborate, collaboration and collaborator.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 labor 衍生 laborious 与 laboratory；laborare 衍生 collaborate、collaboration 与 collaborator。

items.example: The root supplies the toil.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「辛苦」这一层。

items.example: Laborare is the act of working.
items.exampleCN: laborare 是劳动的动作。

items.example: Collaborare joins the prefix to the work.
items.exampleCN: collaborare 把前缀接到劳动上。

items.example: Collaborate is the English verb.
items.exampleCN: collaborate 是英语动词。

items.structure: collaborate plus a suffix of action
items.example: The noun names the joint activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名共同活动。

items.structure: collaborate plus a suffix meaning 'tending to'
items.example: Collaborative describes the arrangement.
items.exampleCN: collaborative 描述这种安排。

items.example: The person who shares the labour.
items.exampleCN: 共同出力的人。

items.structure: laborare plus a suffix of place
items.example: The work place became a research place.
items.exampleCN: 劳作之处变成研究之处。

items.example: To elaborate is to work something out fully.
items.exampleCN: elaborate 就是把某物完全做出来。

definition_zh: 倒塌；崩溃；倒下
definition_en: to fall down suddenly, to fail completely, or to fall down because of illness or weakness
core_image: 一座楼在几秒之内塌成一堆瓦砾
scene: 旧仓库的屋顶在雨里撑不住了。The old roof collapsed under the weight of snow.
sceneCN: 这里 collapse 指「倒塌」（第 1 个义项：突然塌下）；句意是旧屋顶在积雪的重压下塌了。

senses.title: Fall down suddenly
senses.definition: to fall down suddenly because of pressure or a loss of support
senses.definitionCN: 因压力或失去支撑而突然塌下
senses.example: The roof collapsed under the weight of snow.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶在积雪的重压下塌了。
senses.why: The Latin base meant to fall together, which is exactly what a building does.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基意为一起倒下，这正是一栋楼倒塌的样子。

senses.title: Fail completely
senses.definition: to fail suddenly and completely, as a system or a plan does
senses.definitionCN: 像制度或计划那样突然彻底失败
senses.example: The talks collapsed after two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈两小时后破裂了。
senses.why: An argument can fall down like a wall when its supports give way.
senses.whyCN: 论证的支撑一断，也会像墙一样倒下。

senses.title: Fall down from weakness
senses.definition: to fall down suddenly because of illness, injury or tiredness
senses.definitionCN: 因病、受伤或疲劳突然倒下
senses.example: He collapsed at the end of the race.
senses.exampleCN: 他在比赛终点倒下了。
senses.why: The body loses its support just as a structure does.
senses.whyCN: 身体像建筑物一样失去支撑。

intro.en: Collapse comes from Latin collabi, from com- together and labi, to slip or fall.
intro.cn: collapse 出自拉丁语 collabi，由 com-（一起）与 labi（滑落、倒下）组成。

items.en: Labi meant to slip, slide or fall.
items.cn: labi 意为滑、滑落或倒下。

items.en: Collabi described falling down in a heap.
items.cn: collabi 描述塌成一堆。

items.en: The participle collapsus was used of ruined buildings.
items.cn: 分词 collapsus 用于描述毁坏的建筑。

items.en: English collapse first described a building giving way.
items.cn: 英语 collapse 最初描述建筑垮塌。

items.en: Medicine and economics extended it to bodies and systems.
items.cn: 医学与经济学把它扩展到身体与制度。

note.en: The look-alike group holds Latin-shaped words with similar endings, while the meaning group names ways of breaking down or losing strength.
note.cn: 形近组收的是结尾相似、带拉丁形态的词，近义组列出碎裂与失去支撑的说法。

entries.definition: to pass, as time does
entries.definitionCN: 像时间那样流逝

entries.definition: to gather pages into the correct order
entries.definitionCN: 把书页按正确顺序整理

entries.definition: the hiding of the sun or moon by another body
entries.definitionCN: 太阳或月亮被另一天体遮住

entries.definition: to break into small pieces over time
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐碎成小块

entries.definition: to go down below a surface
entries.definitionCN: 沉到表面以下

entries.definition: to lose consciousness for a short time
entries.definitionCN: 短时间失去知觉

normalIntro.en: These hooks work from the Latin picture of falling together, then apply it to walls, plans and bodies.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一起倒下的拉丁画面出发，再挪到墙、计划与身体上。

normal.en: Collapse hides the Latin verb labi, to slip, so the word pictures a slide downward.
normal.cn: collapse 里藏着拉丁动词 labi（滑落），画面就是往下滑。

normal.en: The prefix com- means together, so everything falls at once.
normal.cn: 前缀 com- 意为一起，所以是所有东西同时倒下。

normal.en: A roof, a deal and a runner can all collapse in one second.
normal.cn: 屋顶、交易和奔跑者都可能在刹那间垮掉。

normal.en: Add -ible and collapsible means able to be folded down.
normal.cn: 加上 -ible，collapsible 就是能被折下来的。

normal.en: The noun keeps the same shape as the verb, so no ending is needed.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，不必另加词尾。

abstract.en: Picture a wall folding inward in a cloud of dust.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙在尘土中向内折倒。

abstract.en: Picture a row of numbers on a screen suddenly turning blank.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上的一排数字突然变成空白。

abstract.en: Picture a runner taking one more step and then folding to the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象奔跑者又迈一步，然后蜷倒在地。

examples.en: The bridge collapsed during the storm.
examples.cn: 那座桥在暴风雨中坍塌了。

examples.en: The company collapsed after losing its main investor.
examples.cn: 这家公司在失去主要投资人后垮掉了。

examples.en: She collapsed with tiredness after the long flight.
examples.cn: 长途飞行后她累得倒下了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 collapse 记成 com 加 lapse：所有东西一起滑落，就是塌掉。

root: 源自拉丁语 collabi，com-（一起）加 labi（滑落），本指建筑塌成一堆，后引申为制度失败与身体倒下。

sensesIntro.en: From a roof falling in to a plan breaking down, and then to a body that can no longer stand.
sensesIntro.cn: 从屋顶塌下，到计划破裂，再到再也站不住的身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a structure losing its support and folding into a heap.
core.cn: 核心意象：结构失去支撑，折成一堆。

branches.en: The building sense is the oldest and most physical.
branches.cn: 建筑义最古老，也最具体。

branches.en: A plan fails the way a wall gives way.
branches.cn: 计划失败，就像墙失去支撑。

branches.en: The body sense borrows the same loss of support.
branches.cn: 身体义借用的同样是支撑的丧失。

branches.en: Both a roof and a person can fall in one sudden movement.
branches.cn: 屋顶和人都会在一个突然的动作中倒下。

branches.en: Systems and bodies both need support to keep standing.
branches.cn: 制度与身体都需要支撑才能立住。

intro.en: Collapse belongs to the Latin labi family, which also gives lapse, elapse and relapse.
intro.cn: collapse 属于拉丁语 labi 词族，这一族还给出 lapse、elapse 与 relapse。

latinIntro.en: The base labi, to slip, is the living element behind the whole group.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 labi（滑落）是整组词背后活的成分。

items.meaning: more than one collapse, or it falls down
items.example: The old wall collapses in heavy rain.
items.exampleCN: 这堵旧墙在大雨中塌下。

items.example: The tent collapsed in the wind.
items.exampleCN: 帐篷在风里塌了。

items.example: They fled the collapsing building.
items.exampleCN: 他们逃离了正在倒塌的建筑。

items.meaning: able to be folded or pushed down
items.example: She carried a collapsible cup.
items.exampleCN: 她带着一只可折叠的杯子。

items.meaning: a small failure or a passing of time
items.example: A lapse in attention caused the error.
items.exampleCN: 一次走神造成了这个错误。

items.example: Three hours elapsed before the call came.
items.exampleCN: 三个小时过去，电话才来。

items.meaning: to fall back into illness or a bad habit
items.example: He relapsed after a week of rest.
items.exampleCN: 休息一周后他又复发了。

items.meaning: a body part slipping out of place
items.example: The doctor treated a minor prolapse.
items.exampleCN: 医生治疗了一处轻微的脱垂。

latinEntries.example: Latin collabi is built from com- and labi.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 collabi 由 com- 与 labi 构成。

latinEntries.example: The verb labi also lies behind relapse.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 动词 labi 也藏在 relapse 背后。

definition_zh: v. 核对，校勘；收集并整理（资料、页码）
definition_en: to compare texts carefully and put them in order; to gather and arrange information
core_image: 两份手稿并排摊开，一页页比对
scene: 编辑把两份手稿逐页核对。The editor collated the two manuscripts page by page.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：collate 指核对校勘；句意是编辑把两份手稿逐页核对。

senses.title: To compare texts carefully
senses.definition: to compare copies of a text to find and record differences
senses.definitionCN: 比对文本副本以找出并记录差异
senses.example: Scholars collated the three editions.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们校勘了三个版本。
senses.why: Latin con means together and latus means carried.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 con 意为一起，latus 意为携带。

senses.title: To gather and arrange
senses.definition: to collect information and put it in a clear order
senses.definitionCN: 收集信息并排成清楚次序
senses.example: She collated the survey results into one table.
senses.exampleCN: 她把调查结果汇总成一张表。
senses.why: A comparison of pages became an organising job.
senses.whyCN: 比对页码变成了整理工作。

intro.cn: collate 意为把页面带到一起作比较。

items.cn: con 意为一起。

items.en: Latus is the past participle of ferre, to carry.
items.cn: latus 是 ferre（携带）的过去分词。

items.en: Collatum means brought together.
items.cn: collatum 意为被带到一起。

items.en: Collate names the comparing of manuscripts.
items.cn: 十六世纪 collate 指校勘手稿。

items.en: The verb now covers gathering data too.
items.cn: 现代该动词也指汇总数据。

abstract.en: Two books talking to each other.

abstract.en: Pages looking for their place.
